As he told of Bharata's virtues, his goodness and his nature, Śrī Rāma was lost in an ocean of love.
ayodhya.232.do232: The gods heard Śrī Rāma's words and saw his affection for Bharata,
and all of them praise him: what lord is such a home of grace as Śrī Rāma?
ayodhya.233.cau1: If Bharata had never come into the world, who on earth would carry the yoke of all dharma?
The tale of Bharata's virtues lies beyond the reach of the whole race of poets; O Lord of the Raghus, who but you can know it?
ayodhya.233.cau2: Lakṣmaṇa, Śrī Rāma and Sītā heard what the gods said and felt a joy past all telling.
Here, meanwhile, Bharata and all his companions bathed in the holy Mandākinī.
ayodhya.233.cau3: Leaving all the people by the river, and asking leave of the mothers, the guru and the minister,
Bharata set out for the place where Sītā and Śrī Rāma were, with the Niṣāda chief and his younger brother Śatrughna.
ayodhya.233.cau4: Thinking of what his mother had done, he shrinks with shame, and his mind turns over a million misgivings:
What if Śrī Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa and Sītā hear my name and rise, leave this place and go away somewhere else?
ayodhya.233.do233: If they count me a party to my mother's plan, whatever they do to me will be too little;
yet, mindful of their own nature, they may pardon my sins and faults and receive me kindly.
ayodhya.234.cau1: Whether they cast me off, knowing my heart to be stained, or honour me, taking me for their servant,
my one refuge is Śrī Rāma's sandals. Śrī Rāma is a good master; the fault is wholly the servant's.
ayodhya.234.cau2: The world's praise belongs to the cātaka and the fish, masters of their own vow and love, which with them never grow old.
Pondering thus, he went on along the road, every limb grown slack with shame and love.
ayodhya.234.cau3: It was as though the wrong his mother had done turned him back, yet he, first among the steadfast, went on by the strength of his devotion.
Whenever he called to mind Śrī Rāma's nature, his feet quickened on the path.
ayodhya.234.cau4: What was Bharata's state at that hour? Like the course of a water-beetle in a running stream.
Seeing Bharata's anguish and his love, the Niṣāda chief at that moment lost all sense of his body.
ayodhya.234.do234: Auspicious omens began to appear. Hearing them and weighing them, the Niṣāda chief said:
The anxiety will pass and joy will come, but at the end, sorrow once more.
ayodhya.235.cau1: Knowing all their servant's words to be true, they went on and drew near the hermitage.
Bharata beheld the gathering of woods and hills and rejoiced, like a starving man who has come by good grain.
ayodhya.235.cau2: Like a people worn down by calamities of the season and by fear, tormented by the three kinds of suffering, by malign planets and by pestilence,
who reach a good land under a good king and are at ease: such was Bharata's state.
ayodhya.235.cau3: With Śrī Rāma dwelling there, the riches of the forest shone like a people made happy by a good king.
Dispassion is its minister, discernment its king, and the lovely forest itself the holy land.
ayodhya.235.cau4: Yama and niyama, the restraints and the observances, are its warriors, the mountain its capital; peace and right understanding are its pure and lovely queens.
That good king lacks no limb of a kingdom, and with Śrī Rāma's feet for his support his heart is full of zest.
ayodhya.235.do235: King Discernment has overcome King Delusion and all his army,
and rules his city with no foe left, amid happiness, wealth and seasons of plenty.
ayodhya.236.cau1: Across the forest the sages' dwellings are many, like the cities, towns, villages and hamlets of that kingdom.
Its people are the countless birds of every colour and the beasts of many kinds, a throng beyond describing.
ayodhya.236.cau2: Rhinoceros, elephant, lion, tiger, boar, buffalo and bull: one sees their array and cannot but praise it.
They have laid enmity aside and graze together, here and there, like the four arms of an army.
ayodhya.236.cau3: Waterfalls cascade and elephants in rut trumpet, as though kettledrums of every kind were sounding.
Flocks of cakravākas, cakoras, cātakas, parrots and cuckoos, and graceful swans, call sweetly with glad hearts.
ayodhya.236.cau4: Swarms of bees hum their song and peacocks dance, as though that good reign were keeping festival on every side.
Creepers, trees and grasses all bear fruit and flower; the whole company is a root of joy and blessing.
ayodhya.236.do236: As he gazed on the beauty of Śrī Rāma's mountain, great love filled Bharata's heart,
as an ascetic rejoices when, his vow complete, he gains the fruit of his austerity.
ayodhya.237.cau1: Then the boatman ran and climbed to a height, and raising his arm he said to Bharata:
My lord, there you can see the great trees: pākar, rose-apple, mango and tamāla.
ayodhya.237.cau2: In the midst of those fine trees a banyan stands in its glory, lovely and vast; the heart is charmed to see it.
Its leaves are dark and thick, its fruit is red, and its unbroken shade is pleasant at every season.
ayodhya.237.cau3: It is as though the Creator had gathered up all beauty and shaped from it a mass of darkness flushed with the red of dawn.
Those trees, master, stand by the river, where Śrī Rāma's hut of leaves is built.
ayodhya.237.cau4: Fine tulasī plants of many kinds grow there, set here by Sītā and there by Lakṣmaṇa.
In the banyan's shade an altar has been raised, which Sītā has adorned with her own lotus hands.
ayodhya.237.do237: There each day Sītā and the all-wise Śrī Rāma sit among the sages
and listen to the tales and histories of all the Āgamas, the Vedas and the Purāṇas.
ayodhya.238.cau1: At his friend's words Bharata looked upon the trees, and his eyes brimmed with tears.
The two brothers went on, bowing as they went; even Sarasvatī shrinks from telling of their love.
ayodhya.238.cau2: Seeing the marks of Śrī Rāma's feet, they rejoice like a pauper who has found the philosopher's stone.
They lay the dust on their heads and touch it to their hearts and eyes, and feel a joy like that of meeting Śrī Rāma himself.
ayodhya.238.cau3: Seeing Bharata's state, wholly past telling, beasts and birds and even insentient things were lost in love.
His friend, overcome by love, lost the way; the gods show them the right path and rain down flowers.
ayodhya.238.cau4: The siddhas and seekers who saw it were filled with love and began to praise his natural affection:
Had Bharata's love not been on the earth, who would make the unmoving move and the moving stand still?
ayodhya.238.do238: Love is the nectar, separation the Mandara mountain, and Bharata the deep ocean;
Śrī Rāma, the ocean of mercy, has churned it and brought the nectar forth for the good of gods and saints.
ayodhya.239.cau1: Screened by the thick forest, the charming pair and their friend were hidden from Lakṣmaṇa's sight.
Bharata saw the Lord's holy hermitage, lovely, the dwelling of every blessing.
ayodhya.239.cau2: As he entered, the forest fire of his sorrow died away, as it does for a yogī who attains the supreme truth.
Bharata's eyes fell on Lakṣmaṇa in front of the Lord, telling him with love what he asked.
ayodhya.239.cau3: He has matted locks on his head and a hermit's cloth bound at his waist, his quiver girt on, an arrow in his hand and his bow on his shoulder.
On the altar sits the company of sages and saints, and there with Sītā shines Śrī Rāma.
ayodhya.239.cau4: Śrī Rāma is clad in bark, his hair matted, his body dark; it is as though Rati and Kāma had put on the garb of hermits.
He turns his bow and arrow in his lotus hands, and his smiling glance takes away the burning of the heart.
ayodhya.239.do239: Amid the lovely circle of sages Sītā and Śrī Rāma, the moon of the Raghus, shine
as if, in an assembly of knowledge, Devotion and Being-Consciousness-Bliss sat there in bodily form.
ayodhya.240.cau1: With his younger brother Śatrughna and his friend, Bharata was lost in rapture; joy and grief, pleasure and pain were all forgotten.
Crying, Protect me, my Lord, protect me, master, he fell to the ground like a staff.
ayodhya.240.cau2: Lakṣmaṇa knew him by his loving words, and understood in his heart that Bharata was bowing down.
On this side was the tender love of a brother; on that, the strong pull of the service he owed his master.
ayodhya.240.cau3: He could neither go and embrace him nor leave him unheeded; only a true poet could tell what passed in Lakṣmaṇa's mind.
Service was the side he kept heavy, and he held back, as a flier draws in a kite that has soared aloft.
ayodhya.240.cau4: Bowing his head to the ground, Lakṣmaṇa said with love: O Lord of the Raghus, Bharata is bowing to you.
At these words Śrī Rāma rose, beside himself with love; his robe fell one way, his quiver, bow and arrows another.
ayodhya.240.do240: Śrī Rāma, the treasury of mercy, lifted him up by force and clasped him to his heart.
Seeing Bharata and Śrī Rāma meet, everyone there forgot themselves.
ayodhya.241.cau1: How can the love of that meeting be told? For the whole race of poets it is beyond reach in deed, in mind and in word.
Both brothers are brimming with supreme love, and have forgotten mind, intellect, consciousness and ego.
ayodhya.241.cau2: Say, who can bring such pure love to light? By whose shadow is a poet's mind to follow it?
A poet's true strength lies only in meaning and letters; a dancer dances only to the beat of the rhythm.
ayodhya.241.cau3: The love between Bharata and Śrī Rāma is unfathomable; the minds of Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva cannot reach it.
How then shall I, dull of mind, describe it? Can a fine melody be played on a string of gāṁḍara grass?
ayodhya.241.cau4: Seeing Bharata and Śrī Rāma meet, the gods grew afraid, and their hearts began to pound.
When Bṛhaspati, guru of the gods, reasoned with them, the dull ones came to their senses, and raining flowers they began to sing praises.
ayodhya.241.do241: After meeting Śatrughna lovingly, Śrī Rāma embraced the boatman, the Niṣāda chief.
Lakṣmaṇa bowed to Bharata, and Bharata embraced him with deep feeling.
ayodhya.242.cau1: Lakṣmaṇa eagerly embraced his younger brother, and then clasped the Niṣāda chief to his heart.
Then Bharata and Śatrughna bowed to the sages, and rejoiced to receive the blessings they longed for.
ayodhya.242.cau2: Bharata and his younger brother, in a flood of love, took upon their heads the pollen of Sītā's lotus feet.
As they bowed again and again, she raised them, touched their heads with her lotus hand and seated them.
ayodhya.242.cau3: Sītā gave them her blessing in silence, so lost in love that she had no thought of her body.
Bharata saw that Sītā was well disposed to him in every way; his worry left him, and the groundless dread in his heart passed.
ayodhya.242.cau4: No one says anything and no one asks anything; the mind, full of love, is empty of its own stirring.
At that moment the boatman, the Niṣāda chief, gathered his courage, joined his palms, bowed and made his request:
ayodhya.242.do242: My Lord, with the lord of sages have come all the mothers and the people of the city,
the servants, the commanders and the ministers, all of them distraught at the separation.
ayodhya.243.cau1: Hearing that the guru had come, Śrī Rāma, ocean of gentleness, left Śatrughna beside Sītā,
and at once set off in haste, steadfast, bearer of the yoke of dharma and kind to the lowly.
ayodhya.243.cau2: On seeing the guru, the Lord and his younger brother were overcome with love and began to fall prostrate before him.
The great sage ran forward and clasped them to his heart, and in a surge of love he embraced both brothers.
ayodhya.243.cau3: Then the boatman, thrilling with love, spoke his name and fell prostrate from a distance.
The sage insisted on embracing Śrī Rāma's friend, as if gathering up love that lay rolling on the ground.
ayodhya.243.cau4: Devotion to Śrī Rāma is the root of every blessing: so praising from the sky, the gods rain down flowers.
They say: In lowliness this man has no equal, and in greatness who in the world can equal Vasiṣṭha?
ayodhya.243.do243: That the king of sages, at the sight of him, met him more gladly than he had met even Lakṣmaṇa
is the plain glory and power of worship of Sītā's lord.
ayodhya.244.cau1: Śrī Rāma, the Lord, a mine of compassion who knows all hearts, saw that all the people were in distress.
Whatever the feeling with which each one longed for him, he met each of them in just the way that one wished.
ayodhya.244.cau2: With his younger brother he met everyone in a moment, and took away their dreadful sorrow and burning pain.
This was no great thing for Śrī Rāma: it is as one sun is reflected in ten million pitchers.
ayodhya.244.cau3: Meeting the boatman with overflowing love, all the townspeople praise his good fortune.
Śrī Rāma saw how stricken the mothers were, like rows of lovely creepers blighted by frost.
ayodhya.244.cau4: First of all Śrī Rāma met Kaikeyī, and with his guileless nature and devotion he steeped her mind.
Then, falling at her feet, he consoled her, laying the blame on time, karma and fate.
ayodhya.244.do244: Then Śrī Rāma met all the mothers, comforting them and setting their hearts at ease:
Mother, the world is in the hands of God; one should blame no one.
ayodhya.245.cau1: The two brothers bowed at the feet of the guru's wife, and of the Brahmin women who had come with her.
They honoured them all as they would Gaṅgā and Gaurī, and the women, glad at heart, bless them in gentle words.
ayodhya.245.cau2: Clasping her feet, they clung to Sumitrā's bosom, like a man in utter want who has come upon riches.
Then both brothers fell at their mother's feet, every limb shaken with love.
ayodhya.245.cau3: With great love their mother pressed them to her heart and bathed them in the tears of love that flowed from her eyes.
How is a poet to tell the joy and grief of that hour? As well might the mute tell of a taste.
ayodhya.245.cau4: Having met their mother, Śrī Rāma and his brother asked the guru to come to the hermitage.
Receiving the chief sage's word, the townspeople looked about for water and ground, and made their camp.
ayodhya.245.do245: Taking with them the Brahmins, the ministers, the mothers, the guru and a chosen few,
Bharata, Lakṣmaṇa and Śrī Rāma went to the holy hermitage.
ayodhya.246.cau1: Sītā came and touched the great sage's feet, and received the fitting blessing her heart had asked.
Then she met the guru's wife and the sages' wives with her; the love of that meeting is beyond words.
ayodhya.246.cau2: Sītā bowed at the feet of each one in turn, and was given blessings that gladdened her heart.
When she looked upon all her mothers-in-law, the tender princess shrank and shut her eyes.
ayodhya.246.cau3: They looked like female swans fallen into a fowler's hands. What has the wicked Creator done!
And the queens, gazing at Sītā, felt bitter sorrow: all that fate makes one bear must be borne.
ayodhya.246.cau4: Then Janaka's daughter steadied her heart, her eyes like blue lotuses brimming with tears.
Sītā went and met all her mothers-in-law, and at that moment compassion spread over the earth.
ayodhya.246.do246: Sītā clings to the feet of each in turn and embraces her with deep love,
and they, overcome with love, bless her from the heart: May your married happiness stay full for ever.
ayodhya.247.cau1: Sītā and all the queens were overwhelmed with love; the wise guru asked them all to be seated.
The lord of sages spoke of the illusory course of the world, and told some stories of the highest truth.
ayodhya.247.cau2: Then he told of the king's departure to heaven, and hearing it Śrī Rāma was struck with unbearable grief.
Reflecting that his own love had caused his father's death, he who stands foremost among the steadfast was deeply shaken.
ayodhya.247.cau3: Hearing those bitter words, hard as a thunderbolt, Lakṣmaṇa, Sītā and all the queens wept aloud.
The whole company was distraught with grief, as if the king had died only today.
ayodhya.247.cau4: The great sage comforted Śrī Rāma once more, and he bathed in the holy river with all the company.
That day the Lord kept a fast without even water, and even at the sage's urging no one took a drink.
ayodhya.247.do247: When morning came, whatever the sage directed Śrī Rāma to do,
the Lord carried out all of it with reverence, in faith and devotion.
ayodhya.248.cau1: Having performed the rites for his father as the Vedas lay them down, Śrī Rāma, the sun that dispels the darkness of sin, was made pure.
He whose name is fire to the cotton of sin, and the remembrance of whom is the root of every blessing,
ayodhya.248.cau2: was made pure; the good hold that this was like calling the holy places to come into the Gaṅgā.
When two days had passed after the purification, Śrī Rāma spoke lovingly to the guru:
ayodhya.248.cau3: My Lord, all the people are in great distress, living on nothing but tubers, roots, fruit and water.
When I see Bharata and his brother, the ministers and all the mothers, each moment passes for me like an age.
ayodhya.248.cau4: Please go back to the city with them all; you are here, and the king is in Amarāvatī.
I have said much and been very bold; master, do whatever is right.
ayodhya.248.do248: The guru said: Rāma, bridge of dharma, home of compassion, how should you not speak so?
The people are sorrowing; let them find rest for two days in the sight of you.
ayodhya.249.cau1: At Śrī Rāma's words the company was afraid, like a ship in distress out on the ocean.
Then they heard the guru's words, the root of all good, and it was as though a favourable wind had sprung up.
ayodhya.249.cau2: Thrice daily they bathe in the sacred water; merely to look on it clears away heaps of sin.
They gaze their fill again and again on the Lord, the embodiment of blessing, and joyfully fall prostrate time after time.
ayodhya.249.cau3: They go to see Śrī Rāma's mountain and its forests, where every joy is found and no sorrow at all.
Streams pour down water like nectar, and the breeze of three kinds takes away the three kinds of pain.
ayodhya.249.cau4: There are trees, creepers and grasses of countless kinds, and fruit, flowers and young leaves of many sorts.
There are lovely rocks and the pleasant shade of trees; who could describe the beauty of the forest?
ayodhya.249.do249: In the lakes are lotuses; the water birds call and the bees hum.
Beasts and birds of many colours roam the forest, all enmity gone.
ayodhya.250.cau1: The forest dwellers, the Kols, Kirātas and Bhils, bring honey, pure and fine and sweet as nectar,
filling it into lovely cups they have made of leaves, with bundles of tubers, roots, fruit and shoots.
ayodhya.250.cau2: They offer them to all with humble greetings, telling of each its taste, its kind, its virtues and its name.
People offer a good price, but they will not take it; handing it back, they swear by Śrī Rāma.
ayodhya.250.cau3: Lost in love, they say in gentle words: The good know love when they see it, and honour it.
You are men of merit and we lowly Niṣādas; Śrī Rāma's grace alone has granted us the sight of you.
ayodhya.250.cau4: For us the sight of you is very hard to come by, like a stream of the Gaṅgā in desert land.
The compassionate Śrī Rāma has shown favour to the Niṣāda; as the king is, so should his household and his subjects be.
ayodhya.250.do250: Knowing this in your hearts, set aside your hesitation, see our love and be kind to us;
and to make our lives fulfilled, accept these fruits, grasses and shoots.
ayodhya.251.cau1: You, our dear guests, have set foot in the forest, but we do not have the fortune to be fit to serve you.
What can we give you, master? Firewood and leaves are all that a Kirāta's friendship has to offer.
ayodhya.251.cau2: This is the greatest service we can do: we do not steal your vessels and your clothes.
We are dull creatures who slay living things by the herd, crooked, ill-behaved, ill-minded and of lowly birth.
ayodhya.251.cau3: Our nights and days go by in doing sin; there is no cloth about our waists, and our bellies are never full.
How could a thought of dharma ever have come to us, even in a dream? This is the power of the sight of Śrī Rāma.
ayodhya.251.cau4: Since we set eyes on the Lord's lotus feet, our unbearable sorrows and faults have vanished.
Hearing these words, the people of the city were filled with love and began to praise the good fortune of the forest folk.
ayodhya.251.cha1: All began to praise their fortune and spoke words full of love.
Seeing how they spoke and how they greeted them, and their love for the feet of Sītā and Śrī Rāma, all were glad.
Hearing the words of the Kols and Bhils, the men and women thought little of their own love.
Tulasīdāsa says: it is the grace of Śrī Rāma, jewel of Raghu's line, that the gourd has floated with iron on it.
ayodhya.251.so251: Every day all the people roamed the forest on every side in delight,
as frogs and peacocks grow plump on the water of the first rains.
ayodhya.252.cau1: The men and women of the city were so lost in love that their days slipped by in the blink of an eye.
Sītā took on a separate form for each mother-in-law and served them all with respect, each alike.
ayodhya.252.cau2: No one but Śrī Rāma saw the secret of it; all māyā lies within Sītā's māyā.
Sītā won her mothers-in-law over by her service, and they, made happy, gave her counsel and blessings.
ayodhya.252.cau3: Seeing the two guileless brothers with Sītā, the scheming queen was filled with remorse.
Kaikeyī begged the earth and Yama, but the earth opened no way for her and the Creator granted her no death.
ayodhya.252.cau4: Poets say, as the world and the Vedas also know, that one turned away from Śrī Rāma finds no place even in hell.
In every mind was this one doubt: O Creator, will Śrī Rāma go to Ayodhyā or not?
ayodhya.252.do252: Bharata had no sleep at night and no hunger by day; he was as restless with a pure anxiety
as a fish sunk in the mud at the bottom when the water shrinks.
ayodhya.253.cau1: Bharata thought: Using my mother as a pretext, Time has played a wicked trick, like the dread of a seasonal calamity coming on paddy as it ripens.
In what way can Śrī Rāma be crowned? I can think of not one means.
ayodhya.253.cau2: He would surely come back in obedience to the guru's command, but the sage will speak only once he knows Śrī Rāma's wish.
At his mother's word, too, Śrī Rāma might return; but would Śrī Rāma's mother ever press him?
ayodhya.253.cau3: And what does the word of a servant like me count for? On top of that the times are bad and the Creator is against me.
If I insist, it will be a plain wrong; a servant's duty weighs more than Kailāsa, the mountain of Śiva.
ayodhya.253.cau4: Not one plan held firm in his mind, and Bharata spent the whole night in thought.
In the morning he bathed and bowed his head to the Lord, and he had only just sat down when the sage sent for him.
ayodhya.253.do253: He bowed at the guru's lotus feet and, given leave, sat down.
The Brahmins, the leading citizens, the ministers and all the members of the council came and gathered.
ayodhya.254.cau1: The great sage Vasiṣṭha spoke as the hour required: Listen, members of the council, and you, wise Bharata.
Bearer of the yoke of dharma and sun of the solar line, Śrī Rāma is king; he is the Lord, ruled by none but himself.
ayodhya.254.cau2: He is true to his word and guards the bounds the Vedas set; Śrī Rāma's birth is for the good of the world.
He follows the word of guru, father and mother, crushes the hosts of the wicked and works for the good of the gods.
ayodhya.254.cau3: Right counsel and love, the highest good and one's own good: no one knows them truly as Śrī Rāma does.
Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva, the moon and the sun, the guardians of the quarters, māyā, the soul, all karma and Time,
ayodhya.254.cau4: the king of serpents and the kings of the earth, every lordship there is, and the powers of yoga that the Vedas and scriptures sing of:
weigh it in your minds and see it clearly, Śrī Rāma's command rests on the heads of them all.
ayodhya.254.do254: Our good, every one of us, lies in holding to Śrī Rāma's command and his wish.
Understanding this, you who are wise, now join together and do whatever you all agree upon.
ayodhya.255.cau1: Śrī Rāma's coronation brings joy to all; it is the one path, the root of blessing and gladness.
Consider by what means Śrī Rāma may go to Ayodhyā, and say it; that means is what should be done.
ayodhya.255.cau2: The great sage's words were steeped in right counsel, the highest good and worldly good, and all heard them with respect.
No answer came; the people were at a loss. Then Bharata bowed his head and joined his palms.
ayodhya.255.cau3: Bharata said: Many kings have been born in the solar line, one greater than another.
For all of them a father and a mother are the cause of birth, but it is the Creator who allots good and evil karma.
ayodhya.255.cau4: Your blessing crushes sorrow and brings every good to pass; the whole world knows it.
You, master, are the one who held back even the course of fate; who can undo a resolve that you have made?
ayodhya.255.do255: And now you ask me for a way; all this is my ill fortune.
Hearing these words so full of affection, the guru felt love well up in his heart.
ayodhya.256.cau1: Vasiṣṭha said: Dear son, what you say is true, but it comes by Śrī Rāma's grace alone; turned away from Śrī Rāma, none succeeds even in a dream.
I hesitate, dear son, to say one thing: when everything is slipping away, the wise let half of it go.
ayodhya.256.cau2: You two brothers go to the forest, and let Lakṣmaṇa, Sītā and Śrī Rāma be sent back.
Hearing these welcome words, the two brothers rejoiced, and every limb of theirs was filled with delight.
ayodhya.256.cau3: Their minds were glad and a radiance shone on their bodies, as though the king had come back to life and Śrī Rāma had become king.
The people saw much gain and little loss; but for the queens sorrow and joy weighed the same, and they all wept.
ayodhya.256.cau4: Bharata said: To do what the sage has said would be to give every creature in the world the fruit it longs for.
I will live in the forest all my life; there is no greater comfort for me than this.
ayodhya.256.do256: Śrī Rāma and Sītā know what lies in every heart, and you are all-knowing and wise.
If you mean what you say, my lord, then make your word good.
ayodhya.257.cau1: At Bharata's words and the sight of his love, the sage and the whole council lost all awareness of the body.
Bharata's greatness was a sea; on its shore the sage's mind stood, helpless as a frail woman.
ayodhya.257.cau2: It longs to cross over and searches its heart for a means, but finds no boat, no ship, no raft.
Then who else will sing Bharata's greatness? Does a sea fit inside a pond's shell?
ayodhya.257.cau3: Bharata had won the sage's heart within; the sage came with all the company to Śrī Rāma.
The Lord bowed and gave him a fine seat, and at the sage's bidding everyone sat down.
ayodhya.257.cau4: The great sage spoke considered words, fitted to the place, the time and the occasion:
Listen, Rāma, all-knowing and wise, treasury of dharma, right counsel, virtue and knowledge.
ayodhya.257.do257: You dwell within the hearts of all and know every feeling, good and ill.
Name the course that will bring good to the townspeople, the mothers and Bharata.
ayodhya.258.cau1: Those in distress never speak after weighing their words; a gambler sees only his own throw.
Hearing the sage's words, Śrī Rāma said: My lord, the remedy lies in your own hands.
ayodhya.258.cau2: The good of all lies in keeping to your wish, in doing your bidding and in gladly owning it as right.
First, whatever command is given to me, I will take that counsel on my head and carry it out.
ayodhya.258.cau3: Then, master, whoever you tell to do whatever it may be will set himself to that service in every way.
The sage said: Rāma, what you say is true, but Bharata's love has left me no room to reason.
ayodhya.258.cau4: That is why I say it again and again: my mind has fallen under the sway of Bharata's devotion.
As I see it, whatever is done with Bharata's wish kept will be good, and Śiva is my witness.
ayodhya.258.do258: First listen with respect to Bharata's plea, and then consider it.
Then act on the essence wrung from the view of the good, the view of the people, the policy of kings and the Vedas.
ayodhya.259.cau1: Seeing the guru's love for Bharata, Śrī Rāma felt a special joy in his heart.
Knowing Bharata to be a firm upholder of dharma and his own servant in body, mind and speech,
ayodhya.259.cau2: he spoke words in keeping with the guru's bidding, lovely, gentle and the root of all blessing:
My lord, I swear by you and by my father's feet: no brother like Bharata has ever been born in the world.
ayodhya.259.cau3: Those who love the guru's lotus feet are counted blessed by the world and by the Vedas alike.
Who, then, can tell the fortune of Bharata, on whom you bestow such love?
ayodhya.259.cau4: Since he is my younger brother, my mind shrinks from praising Bharata to his face.
Whatever Bharata says, it will be good to do that. With these words Śrī Rāma fell silent.
ayodhya.259.do259: Then the sage said to Bharata: Dear son, put all hesitation aside,
and tell your dear brother, the ocean of mercy, what is in your heart.
ayodhya.260.cau1: Hearing the sage's words, Bharata learned Śrī Rāma's wish and found guru and master both wholly on his side.
But seeing the whole weight resting on his own head, he could say nothing and only turned the matter over in his mind.
ayodhya.260.cau2: His body thrilling, he stood up before the assembly; his lotus eyes brimmed over with the water of love.
Bharata said: What I had to say, the lord of sages has said for me; what more can I add to it?
ayodhya.260.cau3: I know the nature of my master: he is never angry, even with one who has wronged him.
On me his grace and love are special; never, even at play, have I seen him displeased.
ayodhya.260.cau4: From childhood I have never left his side, and he has never once broken my heart.
I have seen in my heart the way of the Lord's grace: even when I lost at play, he would make me win.
ayodhya.260.do260: I too, held by love and diffidence, have never spoken out before him.
My eyes, thirsty with love, have not had their fill of seeing him to this day.
ayodhya.261.cau1: Fate could not endure how dearly I was loved; base Fate opened a breach, using my mother as the pretext.
Yet even to say this does not become me today; who ever became good and pure by his own reckoning?
ayodhya.261.cau2: My mother is wicked and I am good and upright: to let such a thought into the heart is to be guilty of misconduct ten million times over.
Can an ear of kodo millet bear fine rice? Can a black snail give birth to a pearl?
ayodhya.261.cau3: No one bears a trace of blame, not even in a dream; it is my own misfortune that is a bottomless ocean.
Not seeing that my own sins had ripened into their fruit, I burned my mother with bitter words for nothing.
ayodhya.261.cau4: I have searched my heart and found no way out on any side; only in one way is my good assured.
The guru is my lord, and Sītā and Śrī Rāma are my masters; so the end looks good to me.
ayodhya.261.do261: In this gathering of the good, before the guru and the Lord, on this holy ground, I speak from a sincere heart.
Whether it is love or a sham, false or true, the sage and Śrī Rāma know.
ayodhya.262.cau1: The king held to his vow of love and died for it, and my mother's mind turned to evil: of this the whole world is witness.
The mothers are in a distress no one can bear to look on, and the men and women of the city burn in an unbearable fever.
ayodhya.262.cau2: I alone am the root of all this calamity; hearing it and knowing it, I have borne every pang.
I heard that Śrī Rāma had gone to the forest in the dress of a hermit, with Lakṣmaṇa and Sītā.
ayodhya.262.cau3: They went without shoes, on foot; Śaṅkara is my witness, I lived on even after this wound.
Then, when I saw the Niṣāda's love, even then my heart, hard as a thunderbolt, was not pierced.
ayodhya.262.cau4: Now I have come and seen it all with my own eyes; as long as it lives, this dull soul will make me bear everything.
At the sight of them on the road, she-serpents and scorpions give up their deadly venom and their fierce malice.
ayodhya.262.do262: Those very three, Śrī Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa and Sītā, seemed enemies to her;
whom but her son would fate make bear such unbearable sorrow?
ayodhya.263.cau1: When they heard the noble words of Bharata in his deep distress, blended of anguish, love, humility and right counsel,
all were sunk in grief and the assembly was in turmoil, like a forest of lotuses struck by frost.
ayodhya.263.cau2: The wise sage told many kinds of ancient stories and so consoled Bharata.
Then Śrī Rāma, the moon to the lily-grove of the solar line, spoke fitting words:
ayodhya.263.cau3: Dear brother, it is for nothing that you reproach yourself; know that the course of every being rests with God.
Across the three times and the three worlds, as I see it, all whose fame is holy, dear brother, rank below you.
ayodhya.263.cau4: Whoever so much as thinks you crooked loses this world and is ruined in the next.
Only fools who have never served a guru or sat in the company of the good lay the blame on your mother.
ayodhya.263.do263: Every sin and every snare of the world, the whole load of ill, will be wiped away;
and those who remember your name will win good fame here and happiness in the world to come.
ayodhya.264.cau1: I speak from my heart and speak the truth, with Śiva for witness: Bharata, the earth stands because you uphold it.
Dear brother, do not fall into false reasoning for nothing; enmity and love are not hidden, however one may hide them.
ayodhya.264.cau2: Birds and deer will go right up to a company of sages, and run off when they spot a hunter who means them harm.
Beasts and birds too know who wishes them well and who ill; and the human body is a store of virtue and knowledge.
ayodhya.264.cau3: Dear brother, I know you through and through; yet what can I do, when my heart is torn two ways?
The king held to his word by giving me up, and laid down his life for his vow of love.
ayodhya.264.cau4: To set aside his word troubles my mind, and my regard for you weighs on me still more.
Besides, the guru has given me his command; so whatever you say, that is what I truly wish to do.
ayodhya.264.do264: Be glad at heart, put away your hesitation and tell me; I shall do it this very day.
Hearing these words of Śrī Rāma, who is ever true to his vow, the assembly was glad.
ayodhya.265.cau1: Indra and the hosts of the gods grew fearful and anxious: their cause was about to come to harm.
They could find no remedy that would work, and in their hearts they all took refuge in Śrī Rāma.
ayodhya.265.cau2: Then on reflection they say to one another: Śrī Rāma is ruled by the devotion of his devotee.
When they recalled Ambarīṣa and Durvāsā, the gods and their king lost all hope.
ayodhya.265.cau3: For a long time the gods bore their sorrow; Narasiṁha was made manifest by Prahlāda.
Leaning to one another's ears and beating their heads, they say: Now the gods' cause is in Bharata's hands.
ayodhya.265.cau4: Gods, no other way is to be seen; Śrī Rāma values service done to his true servants.
Let all of you remember Bharata lovingly in your hearts, who wins Śrī Rāma over by his virtues and goodness.
ayodhya.265.do265: Hearing the gods' counsel, Bṛhaspati, guru of the gods, said: Well thought; great is your good fortune.
Of every blessing in the world, love for Bharata's feet is the root.
ayodhya.266.cau1: To serve a servant of Sītā's lord is as rich a blessing as a hundred wish-granting cows.
Devotion to Bharata has entered your minds; leave your worry, for the Creator has set things right.
ayodhya.266.cau2: Lord of the gods, see Bharata's power: Śrī Rāma, by his very nature, cannot help but yield to him.
Steady your hearts, gods; there is nothing to fear. Know Bharata to be Śrī Rāma's shadow.
ayodhya.266.cau3: The Lord, who knows all hearts, heard what the gods and their guru had agreed on and how anxious they were, and he was held back by reluctance.
Bharata knew in his heart that the burden lay on his own head, and turned it over within himself in countless ways.
ayodhya.266.cau4: After thinking it over he settled it in his mind: his own good lay in Śrī Rāma's command.
He said within himself: The Lord gave up his own vow and kept mine; the tenderness and love he has shown me are no small thing.
ayodhya.266.do266: In every way the lord of Sītā has shown me grace beyond all measure.
Then Bharata bowed, and joining his two lotus hands, he spoke:
ayodhya.267.cau1: My master, you are an ocean of mercy and know every heart; what more am I to say now, or have others say for me?
The guru is pleased and my master is kind to me; the pain my soiled mind had made for itself is gone.
ayodhya.267.cau2: I was afraid of a fear of my own making; my worry had no root. Lord, if one loses one's way, the sun is not to blame.
There was my ill fortune, my mother's crookedness, the harsh turn of fate and the cruelty of the times.
ayodhya.267.cau3: All these joined and dug in their feet and laid me waste; but you, protector of all who bow to you, kept your vow.
This is no new way of yours; it is known in the world and in the Veda, and hidden from none.
ayodhya.267.cau4: The world does ill, and you, my master, alone are good; tell me, by whose goodness does anyone come to good?
Lord, your nature is like that of the wish-granting tree: it never leans towards anyone, nor ever turns from anyone.
ayodhya.267.do267: Whoever knows that tree for what it is and goes near it finds that its shade alone stills every care;
and whoever in the world asks of it, king or beggar, good or bad, receives his heart's desire.
ayodhya.268.cau1: Now that I see in every way how the guru and my master love me, my agitation is gone and my mind holds no doubt.
Now, merciful Lord, do only that which will cause your heart no trouble on account of your servant.
ayodhya.268.cau2: A servant who would win his own good by putting his master in a strait has a mean mind.
A servant's good lies in his master's service, done with every comfort and every craving set aside.
ayodhya.268.cau3: My Lord, your return would serve everyone's interest; but in carrying out your command lies good of countless kinds.
This is the essence of worldly gain and of the highest good; this is the fruit of all merit and the ornament of the blessed state.
ayodhya.268.cau4: My Lord, listen first to one plea of mine; after that, do whatever is fitting.
Everything for the coronation has been made ready and brought here; Lord, if your heart consents, let it bear fruit.
ayodhya.268.do268: Send me to the forest with my younger brother, and give all the people their protector;
or else, my Lord, send both brothers back and let me go with you.
ayodhya.269.cau1: Or else let the three of us brothers go to the forest, and you, Lord of the Raghus, go back with Sītā.
Ocean of compassion, do whatever will gladden your heart, my Lord.
ayodhya.269.cau2: Lord, you have laid the whole burden on me; but I have no thought of right counsel or of dharma.
All that I say, I say for my own ends; one in distress has no clear sense left in his mind.
ayodhya.269.cau3: A servant who hears his master's command and answers back — shame itself is ashamed at the sight of him.
Such am I, a fathomless ocean of faults; yet out of love my master praises me as good.
ayodhya.269.cau4: Merciful Lord, the course that pleases me now is the one that leaves my master's heart free of constraint.
I swear by the Lord's feet and speak from a true heart: this is the one way to the good of the world.
ayodhya.269.do269: Whatever command the Lord gives to anyone, with a glad heart and without hesitation,
each will take it on his head and carry it out, and all the trouble and the tangle will be over.
ayodhya.270.cau1: The gods rejoiced at Bharata's pure words; they praised him, crying well done, and showered flowers.
Ayodhyā's people were caught in a dilemma; the ascetics and the forest dwellers felt deep delight.
ayodhya.270.cau2: Śrī Rāma, held back by reluctance, said nothing at all, and seeing the Lord so, the whole assembly grew anxious.
Just then messengers came from Janaka; when he heard of it, the sage Vasiṣṭha sent for them at once.
ayodhya.270.cau3: They bowed and looked upon Śrī Rāma, and at the sight of his dress they were deeply grieved.
The great sage asked the messengers for their news: Tell me, is the king of Videha well?
ayodhya.270.cau4: At this the chief messengers were abashed; they bowed their heads to the ground and, with joined hands, spoke:
Your asking after us with such regard, master, has itself become the cause of our welfare, my lord.
ayodhya.270.do270: Otherwise, my lord, our welfare departed with the lord of Kosala, King Daśaratha.
The whole world has been left without a protector, and Mithilā and Ayodhyā above all.
ayodhya.271.cau1: When they heard what had befallen the lord of Kosala, all the people of Janaka's city were beside themselves with grief.
Whoever saw Videha in that hour, it seemed to none of them that he was truly Videha, one beyond the body.
ayodhya.271.cau2: Hearing of the queen's wicked scheme, the king could see no way, like a snake that has lost its jewel.
Bharata to have the kingdom and Śrī Rāma to be exiled to the forest: at this the lord of Mithilā was deeply dismayed at heart.
ayodhya.271.cau3: The king asked the gathering of wise men and ministers: Think it over and tell me, what is right to do today?
Seeing how things stood in Ayodhyā and the difficulty either way, whether to go or to stay, no one said a word.
ayodhya.271.cau4: Then the king, steadying himself, thought it over in his heart and sent four clever spies to Ayodhyā,
telling them: Find out whether Bharata's intent is true or false, and come back quickly, without being found out.
ayodhya.271.do271: The spies went to Ayodhyā, learned how it was with Bharata and saw what he did;
when Bharata set out for Citrakūṭa, the spies set out for Tirhut.
ayodhya.272.cau1: The spies came back and told Janaka's court of Bharata's conduct as well as they could.
At this the guru, the household, the ministers and the king were all overcome with care and affection.
ayodhya.272.cau2: The king steadied himself, spoke in praise of Bharata, and sent for his finest warriors and the heads of his stables.
Leaving guards for the palace, the city and the realm, he had horses, elephants, chariots and many carriages made ready.
ayodhya.272.cau3: Choosing an auspicious hour, they set out at once, and the king took no rest on the way.
This very morning at daybreak they bathed at Prayāga and went on, and all began to cross the Yamunā.
ayodhya.272.cau4: My lord, we were sent ahead to get news. So saying, they bowed down to the earth.
The great sage gave them six or seven Kirātas to go with them and sent the messengers off at once.
ayodhya.272.do272: When they heard that Janaka was coming, all the company from Ayodhyā rejoiced.
Śrī Rāma was greatly abashed, and Indra, king of the gods, was seized with worry.
ayodhya.273.cau1: The crooked Kaikeyī wastes away with remorse; to whom can she speak, and whom can she blame?
And the men and women are glad as they think: Now it has come about that we shall stay four days more.
ayodhya.273.cau2: So that day too went by; at dawn everyone began to bathe.
After bathing, the men and women worship Gaṇeśa, Gaurī, Śiva the foe of Tripura, and the Sun, the foe of darkness.
ayodhya.273.cau3: Then, bowing to the feet of the Lord of Lakṣmī, they pray with the hems of their garments held in their joined palms:
May Śrī Rāma be king and Jānakī queen, and may Ayodhyā, the capital, be the utmost of joy;
ayodhya.273.cau4: may it be peopled again in happiness with all its folk, and may Śrī Rāma make Bharata crown prince.
O God, water us all with the nectar of this joy, and grant us the reward of living in the world.
ayodhya.273.do273: May Śrī Rāma reign in the city with the guru, the court and his brothers,
and may we die in Ayodhyā while Śrī Rāma is king: this is what everyone asks.
ayodhya.274.cau1: Hearing the loving words of the townspeople, even sages rich in knowledge find fault with yoga and dispassion.
Having done their daily rites in this way, the townspeople bow to Śrī Rāma, thrilling all over.
ayodhya.274.cau2: Men and women of high, low and middle station all have sight of him, each after their own manner.
He takes care to honour every one of them, and all praise the treasury of grace.
ayodhya.274.cau3: Since he was a boy, Śrī Rāma has made it his habit to keep to what is right, discerning where love lies.
Śrī Rāma is an ocean of courtesy and modesty, fair of face, lovely of eye and simple of nature.
ayodhya.274.cau4: Telling over Śrī Rāma's many virtues, they were filled with love, and all began to praise their own good fortune:
Few in the world have such a store of merit as we, whom Śrī Rāma counts as his own.
ayodhya.274.do274: All were lost in love at that moment, when they heard that the lord of Mithilā was coming;
and Śrī Rāma, the sun to the lotus of the solar line, rose in eager haste with all the assembly.
ayodhya.275.cau1: Taking his brothers, the ministers, the guru and the townspeople with him, Śrī Rāma went out ahead.
As soon as Janaka caught sight of the great mountain, he bowed to it and left his chariot then and there.
ayodhya.275.cau2: Such was their longing and zeal to see Śrī Rāma that the strain and hardship of the road did not touch anyone at all.
Their minds were where Śrī Rāma and Vaidehī were; and without the mind, who is aware of the body's pain or ease?
ayodhya.275.cau3: Thus Janaka came on with his company, their minds drunk with love.
When they drew near and saw one another, love welled up in them, and they began to greet one another with respect.
ayodhya.275.cau4: Janaka began bowing at the feet of the sages, and Śrī Rāma paid homage to the seers.
Then Śrī Rāma and his brothers embraced the king and led him on, together with all his company.
ayodhya.275.do275: The hermitage was an ocean brimming with the holy water of the mood of peace,
and the host was like a river of compassion that Śrī Rāma was leading towards it.
ayodhya.276.cau1: It floods the banks of knowledge and dispassion; the words of sorrow are the rivers and streams that run into it.
Sighs of grief are its wind and waves, which break the great trees on the shore of fortitude.
ayodhya.276.cau2: Bitter dejection is its racing current, and fear and bewilderment its numberless whirlpools and eddies.
The wise are the boatmen and learning is a great boat, yet they cannot row across; they cannot even take its measure.
ayodhya.276.cau3: The poor forest folk, the Kols and Kirātas, are travellers who stand still at the sight of it, beaten at heart.
When the river reached the ocean of the hermitage and joined it, the ocean seemed to rise up in turmoil.
ayodhya.276.cau4: Both royal companies were distraught with grief; neither wisdom nor fortitude nor reserve was left to them.
Praising the late king's beauty, virtues and goodness, they weep, sunk deep in the ocean of grief.
ayodhya.276.cha1: Sunk in the ocean of grief, the women and men lament in deep distress,
and all angrily lay the blame, crying: What has perverse Fate done!
Gods, siddhas, ascetics, yogis and sages, on seeing the state Videha was in —
Tulasīdāsa says: not one of them is able to cross the river of love.
ayodhya.276.so276: Here and there the great sages gave the people endless counsel,
and Vasiṣṭha said to Videha: O king, hold fast to your fortitude.
ayodhya.277.cau1: He whose knowledge is a sun that ends the night of worldly existence, whose words are rays at which the lotuses of the sages open —
could delusion and attachment come near him? This is the greatness of love for Sītā and Rāma.
ayodhya.277.cau2: The worldly, the seekers and the wise who have attained: these are the three kinds of beings in the world that the Vedas describe.
He whose heart is moist with love for Śrī Rāma is held in high honour in the assembly of the good.
ayodhya.277.cau3: Knowledge without love for Śrī Rāma has no grace, like a boat with no one at the helm.
The sage consoled Videha in many ways, and all the people bathed at Rāma's ghāṭ.
ayodhya.277.cau4: All the men and women were full of grief, and that day passed without so much as water.
Even the beasts, birds and deer took no food; what need is there to speak of the dear ones and the household?
ayodhya.277.do277: Both companies, and Janaka, king of the line of Nimi, and Śrī Rāma, king of the Raghus, bathed in the morning,
and all sat down beneath the banyan tree, heavy of heart and thin of body.
ayodhya.278.cau1: The Brahmins who lived in Daśaratha's city and those who dwelt in the city of the lord of Mithilā,
the guru of the solar race and Janaka's priest, who had searched out both the ways of the world and the highest truth,
ayodhya.278.cau2: began to give much counsel on dharma, right conduct, dispassion and discernment.
Viśvāmitra told one ancient story after another and consoled the whole assembly with gentle words.
ayodhya.278.cau3: Then Śrī Rāma said to Viśvāmitra: Master, yesterday everyone went without even water.
The sage said: Śrī Rāma speaks rightly; two and a half watches of the day have passed already.
ayodhya.278.cau4: Seeing which way the seer was inclined, the king of Tirhut said: It is not fitting to eat grain here.
What the king said was good, and it pleased everyone; with leave given, they went to bathe.
ayodhya.278.do278: At that moment the forest folk came in great numbers with fruits, flowers, leaves and roots of many kinds,
load upon load filled on their carrying-poles.
ayodhya.279.cau1: By Śrī Rāma's grace the mountains granted every wish, and the mere sight of them took sorrow away.
The lakes, the rivers, the woods and every stretch of land seemed to brim over with joy and love.
ayodhya.279.cau2: Every creeper and tree bore fruit and flower, and birds, beasts and bees made sweet sounds.
At that time the forest was more joyful than ever, and the breeze of three kinds was a joy to all.
ayodhya.279.cau3: Its charm is beyond telling; it was as if the earth were playing host to Janaka.
Then, when all the people had bathed and received leave from Śrī Rāma, Janaka and the sage,
ayodhya.279.cau4: they looked at the fine trees with delight, and the townspeople began to settle here and there.
There were leaves, fruits, roots and tubers of many kinds, pure, fine and like nectar.
ayodhya.279.do279: Śrī Rāma's guru sent them with respect to every one, load after load.
Then, having worshipped the ancestors, the gods, the guests and the guru, they began their meal of fruit.
ayodhya.280.cau1: In this way four days went by, and the men and women were happy gazing on Śrī Rāma.
In the hearts of both companies was this one wish: it would not be good to go back without Sītā and Rāma.
ayodhya.280.cau2: To live in the forest with Sītā and Śrī Rāma is as pleasant as ten million cities of the gods.
Whoever would leave Lakṣmaṇa, Śrī Rāma and Vaidehī and prefer his home, Fate is against him.
ayodhya.280.cau3: Only when fate smiles on all of us can we live in the forest near Śrī Rāma.
To bathe in the Mandākinī at the three times of day and to see Śrī Rāma is a garland of joys and blessings.
ayodhya.280.cau4: To roam Śrī Rāma's hill, the woods and the haunts of ascetics, and to live on tubers, roots and fruit as sweet as nectar:
with such joy, twice seven years would go by like a moment, and no one would feel them pass.
ayodhya.280.do280: All the people say: We are not worthy of such joy; where is fortune like this for us?
Both companies, by their very nature, love the feet of Śrī Rāma.
ayodhya.281.cau1: In this way all of them cherish their wishes, and their loving words, as one hears them, steal the heart.
At that time Sītā's mother sent her maids, and they came back, having seen that the moment was right.
ayodhya.281.cau2: Word came that all of Sītā's mothers-in-law were free, and on hearing it King Janaka's queens came to them.
Kausalyā welcomed them with honour and had seats fit for the occasion brought for them.
ayodhya.281.cau3: All on both sides showed gentleness and love; seeing and hearing it, even the hard thunderbolt would melt.
Their bodies thrilled and limp, their eyes full of tears, they all began to scratch the ground with their nails and to brood.
ayodhya.281.cau4: Every one of them is like an image of love for Sītā and Śrī Rāma, as if compassion herself, taking many forms, were grieving.
Sītā's mother said: The Creator's mind is perverse; he breaks the froth of milk with a chisel of thunderbolt.
ayodhya.281.do281: Nectar is only heard of, but poison is what one sees; all his doings are dreadful.
Everywhere there are crows, owls and herons; swans are found in the Mānasa lake only.
ayodhya.282.cau1: At this Queen Sumitrā spoke in sorrow: Strange indeed is the Creator's course, and wholly contrary.
Having made and nurtured, he takes away again; his judgement is as heedless as a child at play.
ayodhya.282.cau2: Kausalyā said: No one is to blame; it is karma that rules over sorrow and joy, loss and gain.
How karma works is hard to know; the Creator knows it, he who hands out every fruit, good or bad.
ayodhya.282.cau3: The Lord's command rests on every head: on creation, preservation and dissolution, on poison and on nectar too.
O queen, to grieve under the sway of delusion is in vain; the Creator's world is like this, unchanging and without beginning.
ayodhya.282.cau4: My friend, when we dwell in our hearts on the king's life and death and grieve, it is because we see the loss of our own good.
Sītā's mother said: Your gracious words are true; you are the queen of the lord of Avadh, who was himself the very height of the virtuous.
ayodhya.282.do282: Kausalyā said: Let Lakṣmaṇa, Rāma and Sītā go to the forest; the outcome will be good, not ill.
With a full heart she went on: It is Bharata I am anxious about.
ayodhya.283.cau1: My sons and daughters-in-law, by the Lord's favour and your blessing, are like the water of the gods' river.
My friend, I have never once sworn by Rāma; swearing that oath now, I speak from a true heart:
ayodhya.283.cau2: Bharata's gentleness, virtues, humility, greatness, love for his brother, devotion, trust and goodness:
in telling of them even Sarasvatī's mind falters. Can the ocean be emptied with an oyster shell?
ayodhya.283.cau3: Bharata, I have always known, is the lamp of our line; the king said this to me time and again.
The touchstone proves gold, and a jeweller proves a gem; a man is proved, when his hour comes, by his own nature.
ayodhya.283.cau4: It is not fitting for me to speak like this today; in grief and in love, good sense runs thin.
Her words were as cleansing as the Gaṅgā; the queens who heard them were all undone by love.
ayodhya.283.do283: Kausalyā gathered her composure and said: Listen, O queen of Mithilā.
Janaka is a treasury of discernment, and you are his beloved: who is there to give you counsel?
ayodhya.284.cau1: O queen, when you find the moment with the king, put it to him in your own way:
that Lakṣmaṇa be held back and Bharata go to the forest. If the king's mind accepts this counsel,
ayodhya.284.cau2: then let him think it through well and make a proper effort. My anxiety for Bharata is heavy.
Deep and hidden is the love in Bharata's heart; his staying behind does not seem right to me.
ayodhya.284.cau3: Seeing her nature and hearing her simple, gracious words, all the queens were steeped in the mood of pathos.
Flowers rained from the sky and cries of Blessed, blessed! rang out. Siddhas, yogis and sages went limp with love.
ayodhya.284.cau4: All the queens' company stood still as they watched; then Sumitrā collected herself and said:
O queen, two ghaṛīs (some forty-eight minutes) of the night are gone. Hearing this, Śrī Rāma's mother rose with affection
ayodhya.284.do284: and with love and sincerity said: Do not delay; go back now to your own lodging.
We have no one now but the Lord to turn to, unless it be the lord of Mithilā to help us.
ayodhya.285.cau1: Seeing that love and hearing those humble words, Janaka's beloved clasped Kausalyā's holy feet.
She said: O queen, such humility is fitting in you, the wife of Daśaratha and the mother of Śrī Rāma.
ayodhya.285.cau2: The great honour even those beneath them: fire carries smoke on its head, and a mountain carries grass.
Our king is your servant in deed, mind and word; your helpers at all times are Śiva and Bhavānī.
ayodhya.285.cau3: Who in the world is fit to stand at your side as helper? Does a lamp look well as the sun's helper?
Śrī Rāma will go to the forest, do the gods' work, and then reign unshaken in Avadhapura.
ayodhya.285.cau4: Gods, nāgas and men, by the might of Śrī Rāma's arms, will live in happiness, each in his own realm.
All this the sage Yājñavalkya has already foretold, and a sage's word, O queen, does not prove false.
ayodhya.285.do285: With these words she bowed at Kausalyā's feet in great love and put forward her plea for Sītā;
then, given kind leave, Sītā's mother went away with Sītā beside her.
ayodhya.286.cau1: Vaidehī met her dear kinsfolk, each in the manner fitting for each.
Seeing Jānakī in an ascetic's dress, all were thrown into distress by an especially deep sorrow.
ayodhya.286.cau2: With the leave of Śrī Rāma's guru Janaka set out for the camp, and on arriving he saw Sītā.
Janaka clasped to his heart Jānakī, the guest of his pure love and of his very life.
ayodhya.286.cau3: An ocean of love surged up in his heart, and the king's mind became, as it were, Prayāga.
In it he saw the banyan of love for Sītā growing, and on it shone the child of love for Śrī Rāma.
ayodhya.286.cau4: It was as if his knowledge, the long-lived sage, distraught and drowning, had found the support of that child.
Videha's mind is not sunk in delusion; this is the glory of love for Sītā and Śrī Rāma.
ayodhya.286.do286: Love for her father and mother left Sītā so shaken that she could not hold herself together.
Then the daughter of the Earth, weighing the moment and what was right, took hold of her courage.
ayodhya.287.cau1: Seeing Sītā in an ascetic's dress, Janaka felt a special love and contentment.
Janaka said: Daughter, you have made both families holy; everyone says that your bright fame has made the world shine white.
ayodhya.287.cau2: The river of your fame has outdone the Gaṅgā and flowed on through ten million universes.
The Gaṅgā made three places on earth great; this river has made many gatherings of the good great.
ayodhya.287.cau3: Her father spoke true and gracious words in love, and Sītā seemed to melt into shyness.
Then father and mother held her to their hearts and gave her fine counsel and blessings for her good.
ayodhya.287.cau4: Sītā does not say it, but in her heart she hesitates: to stay here for the night is not right.
Seeing how she felt, the queen let the king know, and in their hearts both praise her gentleness and nature.
ayodhya.287.do287: Again and again they held and embraced her, and then with honour bade Sītā farewell.
Then, finding the moment, the wise and sweet-spoken queen told the king of Bharata's state.
ayodhya.288.cau1: Hearing of Bharata's conduct, which was like fragrance in gold and like nectar, the essence of the moon, the king
closed his tear-filled eyes; his body thrilled, and with a glad heart he began to praise Bharata's fair fame.
ayodhya.288.cau2: Janaka said: Fair-faced, lovely-eyed one, hear me with care; the tale of Bharata releases one from the fetters of worldly life.
Dharma, the ways of kings, the inquiry into Brahman: in these I can move about as far as my understanding allows.
ayodhya.288.cau3: That same mind of mine, what could it say of Bharata's glory? Not even by some trick does it touch its shadow.
Brahmā, Gaṇeśa, Śeṣa, Śiva, Sarasvatī, poets, scholars, the wise and those skilled in judgement:
ayodhya.288.cau4: to every one of them Bharata's deeds, fame, actions, dharma, gentleness, virtues and spotless glory
bring joy to understand and to hear; in purity they put the Gaṅgā to shame, and in sweetness even nectar.
ayodhya.288.do288: Bharata is a man of boundless virtues, beyond compare; know that the only one like Bharata is Bharata.
Can Mount Sumeru be called equal to a ser weight? So even the minds of the poets have held back.
ayodhya.289.cau1: To describe it, O lovely one, is beyond everyone, as moving on dry land is for a fish without water.
Bharata's glory has no measure, O queen, hear me: Śrī Rāma knows it, but cannot put it into words.
ayodhya.289.cau2: When he had spoken with love of Bharata's greatness, the king, seeing what his wife's heart desired, said:
That Lakṣmaṇa should return and Bharata go to the forest is for the good of all, and it is in everyone's mind.
ayodhya.289.cau3: But, O queen, the love and trust between Bharata and Śrī Rāma cannot be reached by reasoning.
Bharata is the farthest bound of love and attachment, though Śrī Rāma is the farthest bound of even-mindedness.
ayodhya.289.cau4: The highest good, worldly gain and every pleasure: Bharata has not looked at them even in a dream, even in thought.
Love for Śrī Rāma's feet is the means and that same love the attainment; this, as I see it, is Bharata's creed.
ayodhya.289.do289: Bharata will never set aside Śrī Rāma's command, not even by mistake, not even in thought.
So do not let love make you anxious, said the king, his voice breaking.
ayodhya.290.cau1: Lovingly the couple went over the virtues of Śrī Rāma and Bharata, and for them the night was gone in the space of a blink.
In the morning the two royal companies rose; each person bathed and turned to the worship of the gods.
ayodhya.290.cau2: Śrī Rāma bathed and went to the guru, bowed at his feet and, sensing his assent, spoke:
My lord, Bharata, the people of the city and the mothers are distraught with grief and suffering in this forest life.
ayodhya.290.cau3: With all his company the king of Mithilā has borne hardship now for many days.
My lord, do what is fitting; everyone's good rests in your hands.
ayodhya.290.cau4: Having said this, Śrī Rāma was deeply abashed; the sage thrilled all over to see his gentleness and nature.
The sage said: Rāma, without you every comfort and provision is like hell to both royal companies.
ayodhya.290.do290: Rāma, you are the very life of life, the soul of the soul and the joy of joy.
Dear one, those who leave you and find their homes pleasing have the Creator against them.
ayodhya.291.cau1: May such happiness, such karma and such dharma be burnt to ashes, where Śrī Rāma's lotus feet are not loved.
Yoga turns to bad yoga and knowledge to ignorance where love for Śrī Rāma does not come first.
ayodhya.291.cau2: Without you all are in sorrow, and those who are happy are happy through you alone; you know whatever is in the heart of each.
Your command rests on every head, and you, the compassionate one, know well how it stands with everyone.
ayodhya.291.cau3: Now go to your hermitage. With these words the great sage grew faint with love.
Then Śrī Rāma bowed and went away, and the sage, steadying himself, came to Janaka.
ayodhya.291.cau4: The guru repeated Śrī Rāma's words to the king, words made lovely by courtesy, affection and his natural goodness.
Great king, now do that very thing by which the good of all comes about, and dharma with it.
ayodhya.291.do291: O king, you are a treasury of knowledge, wise, pure and steadfast in dharma.
Without you, who could put this dilemma to rest at such a time?
ayodhya.292.cau1: Hearing the sage's words, Janaka was overcome with love; seeing his state, knowledge and dispassion themselves grew detached.
Weak with love, he turns it over in his mind: our coming here was not well done.
ayodhya.292.cau2: Daśaratha bade Śrī Rāma go to the forest, and himself proved true his love for the one he held dear.
Now we are to send him on from one forest to another and go home rejoicing: such is the greatness of our discernment.
ayodhya.292.cau3: The ascetics, sages and Brahmins who heard and saw this were overcome by love and deeply moved.
Seeing what the hour required, King Janaka took heart and went with his company to Bharata.
ayodhya.292.cau4: Bharata came forward to receive them and gave them fine seats as the occasion required.
The king of Tirhut said: Dear Bharata, you know Śrī Rāma's nature.
ayodhya.292.do292: Śrī Rāma keeps his vow of truth and holds fast to dharma, and has regard and affection for all.
Held back by reserve, he bears this hardship. Tell us what command you would give.
ayodhya.293.cau1: Hearing this, his body thrilling and his eyes filled with tears, Bharata gathered great composure and spoke:
My lord, you are dear to me and revered as a father; and not even a mother or a father wishes us such good as our family guru.
ayodhya.293.cau2: Viśvāmitra and the other sages sit here with the ministers, and the ocean of knowledge today is you yourself.
Master, know me for a child, a servant who follows your command, and give me your counsel.
ayodhya.293.cau3: In such an assembly and such a place, you ask me? If I keep silent I am base, and if I speak I am mad.
I speak big words with a small mouth; father, forgive me, for you see the Creator has turned against me.
ayodhya.293.cau4: That service is a hard duty is famed in the Āgamas, the Vedas and the Purāṇas, and everyone in the world knows it.
A servant's duty to his master is at odds with his own interest; enmity is blind, and love is never clear-sighted.
ayodhya.293.do293: So, keeping to Śrī Rāma's wish, to dharma and the vow, and knowing me to be dependent on another,
and with the love in view, do what all agree to and what is for the good of all.
ayodhya.294.cau1: When the king heard what Bharata said and saw his nature, he and all his company spoke in praise of him.
His words were easy and yet beyond reach, gentle and lovely and yet hard; few in letters, boundless in meaning.
ayodhya.294.cau2: As a face in a mirror cannot be grasped, though the mirror is in one's own hand, so was that wondrous speech beyond grasping.
The king, Bharata and the sage went with the company to where Śrī Rāma was, the moon to the night-lilies that are the gods.
ayodhya.294.cau3: Hearing the news, all the people were troubled with anxiety, like shoals of fish when the new water comes.
The gods looked first at the family guru and how he was, then at the surpassing love of Janaka, king of Videha.
ayodhya.294.cau4: They saw Bharata, all devotion to Śrī Rāma, and the self-seeking gods trembled and gave up hope in their hearts.
Finding all of them steeped in love for Śrī Rāma, the gods fell into an anxiety beyond reckoning.
ayodhya.294.do294: Indra, king of the gods, said in his anxiety: Śrī Rāma is held by affection and reserve.
Band together, all of you, and contrive some trick; if not, the harm is already done.
ayodhya.295.cau1: The gods called Sarasvatī to mind and praised her: Goddess, we gods have come to you for refuge; protect us.
Turn Bharata's mind by your māyā; cast a shade of deceit and so shelter the race of gods.
ayodhya.295.cau2: Hearing the prayer of the gods, and knowing them to be dull-witted with self-interest, the wise goddess said:
You ask me to turn Bharata's mind? With a thousand eyes you cannot see Mount Sumeru.
ayodhya.295.cau3: The māyā of Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva is mighty indeed, yet even it cannot so much as look upon Bharata's mind.
And you ask me to lead that mind astray? Could moonlight ever rob the fierce-rayed sun?
ayodhya.295.cau4: Sītā and Śrī Rāma dwell in Bharata's heart; can there be darkness where the light of the sun shines?
With these words Sarasvatī left for Brahmā's realm; the gods were left in distress, like cakravāka birds when night falls.
ayodhya.295.do295: The self-seeking gods, their minds unclean, took evil counsel and laid an evil plan;
they wove a snare and spread a mighty māyā of fear, confusion, discontent and a longing to be gone.
ayodhya.296.cau1: Having played his wicked trick, Indra still fretted, for the success or ruin of it all lay in Bharata's hands.
Janaka came near to Śrī Rāma, and the lamp of the solar line honoured everyone.
ayodhya.296.cau2: In words at odds with neither the hour, the assembly nor dharma, the priest of the Raghus then spoke.
He gave an account of what Janaka and Bharata had said to each other, and then of the lovely words Bharata had spoken.
ayodhya.296.cau3: Dear Rāma, whatever command you give, let all do just that; this is my view.
Hearing this, Śrī Rāma joined both his palms and spoke words true, simple and gentle:
ayodhya.296.cau4: While you and the king of Mithilā are here, for me to speak would be unseemly in every way.
Whatever you and the king command, I swear by you, shall truly be taken upon the head.
ayodhya.296.do296: At Śrī Rāma's oath, the sage, Janaka and the whole assembly were abashed.
All looked to Bharata's face; no one could find an answer to give.
ayodhya.297.cau1: Bharata saw the assembly bound by reserve; then he, Śrī Rāma's brother, summoned great composure,
and, seeing the hour was hard, held back his love, as Agastya checked the rising Vindhya.
ayodhya.297.cau2: Grief, like Hiraṇyākṣa, had carried off the earth of understanding, the womb from which the host of pure virtues springs.
Bharata's discernment, like the mighty Boar, lifted it out at that moment without effort.
ayodhya.297.cau3: He bowed to all with joined palms and entreated Śrī Rāma, the king, the guru and the saints:
Forgive me today this great impropriety: with a tender mouth I speak hard words.
ayodhya.297.cau4: In his heart Bharata remembered gracious Sarasvatī; leaving his mind, her Mānasa lake, she came to the lotus of his mouth.
Bharata's speech is a graceful swan, rich in pure discernment, dharma and wise conduct.
ayodhya.297.do297: Seeing with the eyes of discernment the whole assembly faint with love,
Bharata bowed and, with Sītā and Śrī Rāma in his thoughts, spoke:
ayodhya.298.cau1: My Lord, you are my father, mother, friend, guru and master; revered, my truest well-wisher, the knower of all hearts;
guileless, a good master, a treasury of kindness, the protector of those who bow to you, all-knowing and wise;
ayodhya.298.cau2: mighty, the benefactor of those who seek your refuge, one who prizes merit and takes away faults and sins.
Master, the only master like you is you; and in betraying my master the only one like me is I.
ayodhya.298.cau3: Swayed by delusion, I set aside the word of my Lord and of my father, and came here with a gathering at my back.
In the world there are good and bad, high and low, nectar and the state of the immortals, poison and death;
ayodhya.298.cau4: but one who would cancel Śrī Rāma's command even in thought has never been seen or heard of anywhere.
That very insolence I committed in every way, and the Lord took it for love and service.
ayodhya.298.do298: My Lord, by your own grace and goodness you have done me good;
my faults became like ornaments, and fair renown spread on every side.
ayodhya.299.cau1: Your ways, your good nature, your greatness: the world knows them, and the Vedas and Āgamas sing them.
The cruel, the crooked, the wicked, the evil-minded, the disgraced, the base, the graceless, the godless and the reckless:
ayodhya.299.cau2: they too, hearing of your refuge, came before you, and you made them your own when they had bowed but once.
Seeing their faults, you never took them to heart; hearing of their virtues, you praised them among the company of saints.
ayodhya.299.cau3: What master is there who favours his servant and himself sets in order all that the servant needs,
who never, even in a dream, counts what he himself has done, but carries in his own heart his servant's reserve and care?
ayodhya.299.cau4: That master is no other than you; I say it with my arm raised, staking my word.
A beast that dances, a parrot skilled in reciting: their skill and their ways depend on the showman and the teacher.
ayodhya.299.do299: In this way you have set your servants right, honoured them and made them the crown of the saints.
Who but the compassionate Lord would keep up his roll of glory with such strength?
ayodhya.300.cau1: Whether from grief, from love or from a child's nature, I came here with your command set aside.
Even then the compassionate Lord, looking to his own nature, took all I did as good in every way.
ayodhya.300.cau2: I have seen your feet, the root of all that is auspicious, and learned that my master is by nature kind to me.
In this great assembly I have seen my fortune: for all my great fault, my master's love.
ayodhya.300.cau3: The treasury of mercy has shown me grace and favour wholly and to the full, and more than enough in everything.
My master has kept up his fondness for me, out of his own kindness, nature and goodness.
ayodhya.300.cau4: My Lord, I have been utterly bold, casting off all reserve before my master and the assembly.
Rude or humble, I have spoken as I pleased; my Lord will forgive me, knowing how deep my distress is.
ayodhya.300.do300: To say much to a friend so wise and a master so good is a great fault.
So give me your command now, my Lord; you have set all my affairs right.
ayodhya.301.cau1: I swear by the pollen of the Lord's lotus feet, the lovely bound of truth, merit and joy.
On that oath I tell the wish of my own heart, the wish it holds waking, sleeping and in dreams.
ayodhya.301.cau2: That wish is this: to serve my master in simple love, setting aside self-interest, guile and the four rewards of life.
No service of a good master equals obeying his command; may your servant receive that grace, my Lord.
ayodhya.301.cau3: Having said this, Bharata was utterly overcome by love; his body thrilled and his eyes filled with tears.
In his distress he clasped the Lord's lotus feet; that moment and that love cannot be told.
ayodhya.301.cau4: The ocean of mercy honoured him with gentle words, drew him close by the hand and had him sit beside him.
Hearing Bharata's plea and seeing his nature, the whole assembly and Śrī Rāma went limp with love.
ayodhya.301.cha1: Śrī Rāma, the company of saints, the sages and the lord of Mithilā were all limp with love;
in their hearts they praised the boundless glory of Bharata's love for his brother and of his devotion.
The gods praised Bharata and rained down flowers, but their minds were as if soiled.
Tulasīdāsa says: hearing this, all the people grew troubled and shrank like lotuses at nightfall.
ayodhya.301.so301: Seeing all the men and women of both companies sorrowful and forlorn,
Indra, foul of heart, seeks his own good by killing those already dead.
ayodhya.302.cau1: The king of the gods is the very limit of guile and crooked ways; he loves another's loss and his own gain.
Indra, foe of Pāka, has a crow's ways: deceitful and foul, he trusts no one anywhere.
ayodhya.302.cau2: First he laid an evil plan and gathered his guile; then he cast that spell of restlessness on everyone's head.
The gods' māyā bewildered all the people, yet they were not wholly cut off from their love for Śrī Rāma.
ayodhya.302.cau3: Gripped by fear and restlessness, no mind is steady; one moment they long for the forest, the next their homes appeal.
Their minds pulled two ways, the people are wretched, like the water where a river meets the sea.
ayodhya.302.cau4: Torn in two, they find no peace anywhere, and none tells another what is in his heart.
Seeing this, the treasury of compassion laughed within and said: a dog, Indra and a young man are of one kind.
ayodhya.302.do302: Leaving out Bharata, Janaka, the sages, the ministers and the clear-minded saints,
the gods' māyā took hold of everyone else, as if it had found each one as each was fit.
ayodhya.303.cau1: The ocean of mercy saw the people distressed by their own love and by Indra's heavy deceit.
The assembly, the king, the guru, the Brahmins and the ministers: the minds of all were held fast by Bharata's devotion.
ayodhya.303.cau2: They gaze at Śrī Rāma like figures in a painting, and speak shyly, as if repeating words they had been taught.
Bharata's love, humility, courtesy and greatness are a joy to hear, but hard to describe.
ayodhya.303.cau3: Bharata, at the merest trace of whose devotion the sages and the lord of Mithilā were lost in love:
how can Tulasīdāsa tell of his glory? By the nature of devotion, a good understanding has welled up in his heart.
ayodhya.303.cau4: But knowing itself small and that glory great, and in deference to the company of poets, it shrank back.
Its eagerness is great, yet it cannot tell those virtues; the mind moves like the words of a child.
ayodhya.303.do303: Bharata's spotless fame is a spotless moon, and good understanding a young cakora bird;
the moon has risen in the clear sky of the devotees' hearts, and she gazes at it without blinking.
ayodhya.304.cau1: Bharata's nature is not easy to grasp even for the Vedas; may the poets forgive the rashness of my little mind.
Who, telling or hearing of Bharata's true feeling, would not come to love the feet of Sītā and Rāma?
ayodhya.304.cau2: If one remembers Bharata and love for Śrī Rāma still does not come easily to him, who is as ill-fated as he?
The compassionate and all-knowing Śrī Rāma saw the state of everyone and knew what was in his devotee's heart.
ayodhya.304.cau3: He is the upholder of dharma, steadfast, wise in right conduct, an ocean of truth, love, good nature and joy.
Śrī Rāma, guardian of right counsel and of love, weighed the place, the time, the occasion and the gathering,
ayodhya.304.cau4: and spoke words that seemed to hold all the wealth of speech, bringing good in the end and, to the ear, like the moon's nectar:
Dear Bharata, you are the upholder of dharma, knowing in the ways of the world and the Veda, and skilled in love.
ayodhya.304.do304: In deed, word and mind you are pure; dear brother, you alone are your own equal.
Among the elders, and at so hard a time, how can a younger brother's virtues be told?
ayodhya.305.cau1: Dear brother, you know the custom of the Sun's line, and the fame and the love of our father, who was true to his word;
you know the time, the gathering and the regard owed to elders, and the minds of the indifferent, of friends and of foes.
ayodhya.305.cau2: You know what each one must do, and the dharma that is the highest good for you and for me.
I trust you in every way; still, I will say what the moment calls for.
ayodhya.305.cau3: Dear brother, with our father gone, our affairs have been held together only by the grace of the guru's house.
Otherwise the people, the kinsfolk and the household, all of us with them, would have been ruined.
ayodhya.305.cau4: If the sun were to set before its time, tell me, who in the world would not suffer?
Such a disaster, dear brother, is what fate has wrought; yet the sage and the lord of Mithilā have kept everything safe.
ayodhya.305.do305: The work of the kingdom, our honour and good name, dharma, land, wealth and homes:
the guru's power will protect them all, and the end will be good.
ayodhya.306.cau1: For your company and mine, at home or in the forest, the guru's grace is our guard.
The command of mother, father, guru and master is Śeṣa, who bears up the whole earth of dharma.
ayodhya.306.cau2: So carry it out yourself and see that I do too; dear brother, be the guardian of the Sun's line.
To one who strives, this alone grants every success; it is a meeting of three streams, rich in fame, a blessed end and prosperity.
ayodhya.306.cau3: Bearing this in mind, endure the heavy hardship and keep the people and the family happy.
