a thousand Śeṣas could not describe, for there Śrī Rāma reigns as king.
uttar.27.cau1: Nārada, Sanaka and other great sages, to see the Lord of Kosala,
come to Ayodhyā every day, and at the sight of the city they forget their dispassion.
uttar.27.cau2: The upper storeys are built of gold and gems, with lovely floors cast in many colours.
Round the city runs a wall of great beauty, crowned with fine battlements of every colour.
uttar.27.cau3: It is as if the hosts of the nine planets had formed an army and come to lay siege to Amarāvatī.
The ground is paved with glass of many colours, and seeing it even the minds of great sages dance.
uttar.27.cau4: The white mansions kiss the sky above, and their pinnacles seem to scorn the brilliance of the sun and moon.
Windows wrought of many gems sparkle, and in every house lamps of gems glow.
uttar.27.cha1: Lamps of gems shine, the mansions gleam, and the thresholds are made of coral.
There are pillars of gems, and walls fashioned by Brahmā himself, inlaid with gold, gems and emeralds.
The mansions are beautiful, charming and spacious, and their courtyards are built of lovely crystal.
At every single gateway the doors are of gold, finely wrought and set with many diamonds.
uttar.27.do27: In every house there are lovely picture halls, where the deeds of Śrī Rāma are painted with great art;
any sage who gazes at them has his heart stolen away.
uttar.28.cau1: Everyone has planted flower gardens and laid them out with care in many styles.
In them graceful creepers of many kinds, lovely to see, are always in bloom, as if it were spring.
uttar.28.cau2: Bees hum with a sweet and charming sound, and a pleasant breeze, cool, gentle and fragrant, is always blowing.
Children have reared birds of many kinds, which speak sweetly and look lovely as they fly.
uttar.28.cau3: Peacocks, swans, cranes and pigeons look splendid upon the mansions.
Seeing their own reflections here and there, they call in many ways and dance.
uttar.28.cau4: Children teach the parrots and mynas: Say Rāma, Raghupati, protector of his people.
The royal gateway is beautiful in every way, and so are the streets, the crossroads and the markets.
uttar.28.cha1: The lovely markets are beyond describing; there goods are had without payment.
Where he in whom Ramā dwells is himself king, how could the wealth of the place be sung?
Cloth dealers, bankers and many merchants sit there, as though each were Kubera.
Women, men, children and the old, whoever they are, are all happy, all upright and fair to see.
uttar.28.do28: On the northern side flows the Sarayū, its water clear and deep.
Charming ghats are built along it, and there is not the least mud on its banks.
uttar.29.cau1: Far off, in an open place, is a fine ghat where troops of horses and elephants drink.
There are many ghats for drawing water, most charming, and there men do not bathe.
uttar.29.cau2: The royal ghat is fine and beautiful in every way; there men of all four varṇas bathe.
All along the bank stand temples of the gods, with lovely groves on every side of them.
uttar.29.cau3: At spots along the riverside dwell sages and renunciants who have turned from the world and delight in knowledge.
Lovely tulasī lines the banks, set out clump by clump by many sages.
uttar.29.cau4: The beauty of the city cannot be told at all, and outside the city too all is supremely lovely.
At the sight of the city every sin takes flight; there are woods, groves, stepwells and lakes.
uttar.29.cha1: Peerless stepwells, lakes and wells, charming and wide, add to its beauty.
Seeing their fine steps and clear water, gods and sages are entranced.
Lotuses of many colours grow there, many birds call and bees hum.
The delightful gardens, with the songs of cuckoos and other birds, seem to call out to the passers-by.
uttar.29.do29: Can the city whose king is the Lord of Ramā be described?
Aṇimā and the other powers, and all joys and riches, fill the whole of Ayodhyā.
uttar.30.cau1: Everywhere people sing Śrī Rāma's virtues, and as they sit together they urge this upon one another:
Worship Śrī Rāma, who cherishes those who bow to him, the home of beauty, good character, grace of form and every virtue.
uttar.30.cau2: Worship him whose eyes are lotuses and whose body is dark, who guards his servants as the eyelids guard the eyes.
Worship him who bears lovely arrows, bow and quiver, the sun to the lotus grove of the saints, steadfast in battle.
uttar.30.cau3: Worship him who is Garuḍa to the terrible serpent of Time, who wipes out the sense of mine in all who bow to him free of desire.
Worship him who is the hunter of the herd of deer, greed and delusion, a lion to the elephant of desire, and the giver of joy to his devotees.
uttar.30.cau4: He is the sun to the thick darkness of doubt and grief, and the fire that burns the dense forest of the demons.
Why do you not worship Śrī Rāma, together with Janaka's daughter, who shatters the fear of worldly existence?
uttar.30.cau5: He is a mass of frost to the mosquitoes of countless desires; he is ever the same, unborn and imperishable.
Worship the delight of the sages, who takes away the burden of the earth, the generous Lord of Tulasīdāsa.
uttar.30.do30: In this way the women and men of the city sing the praises of Śrī Rāma,
and the Lord, treasury of compassion, is ever gracious to them all.
uttar.31.cau1: Garuḍa, ever since the mighty sun of Śrī Rāma's glory rose,
its light has filled the three worlds; to many it has brought joy, and to many grief of heart.
uttar.31.cau2: I shall tell you in full of those who grieve. First, the night of ignorance came to an end.
The owls of sin hid wherever they could, and the white lilies of desire and anger shrank shut.
uttar.31.cau3: Actions of many kinds, the guṇas, time and one's nature: these cakora birds never find any joy.
Envy, vanity, delusion and pride are thieves whose craft succeeds in no direction.
uttar.31.cau4: In the lake of dharma the lotuses of knowledge and realised knowledge opened in many ways.
Happiness, contentment, dispassion and discernment, these many cakravāka birds, were freed from grief.
uttar.31.do31: When this sun of glory shines in anyone's heart,
those named last grow strong, and those named first are destroyed.
uttar.32.cau1: Once Śrī Rāma, with his brothers and with Hanumān, son of the Wind, most dear to him,
went to see a beautiful grove; every tree was in flower and covered in fresh leaves.
uttar.32.cau2: Knowing it to be the right time, Sanaka and his brothers came, masses of radiance, graced with virtue and good character.
They are ever absorbed in the bliss of Brahman; to look at they are children, yet they are of great age.
uttar.32.cau3: They seem the four Vedas in bodily form; these sages see all alike and are free of all sense of difference.
The quarters of the sky are their only clothing, and their one passion is to listen wherever the deeds of Śrī Rāma are being told.
uttar.32.cau4: Bhavānī, Sanaka and his brothers had been staying where the wise and great sage Agastya, the pot-born, lives.
The great sage had told the story of Śrī Rāma at length; from it knowledge is born, as fire is born from the fire-sticks.
uttar.32.do32: Seeing the sages coming, Śrī Rāma joyfully prostrated himself before them.
Welcoming them and asking after their well-being, the Lord gave them his own yellow robe to sit on.
uttar.33.cau1: The three brothers too, with Hanumān, son of the Wind, prostrated themselves, and their joy was great.
The sages gazed on Śrī Rāma's matchless beauty and were lost in it; they could not hold their minds back.
uttar.33.cau2: Dark of body, with lotus eyes, he is the home of beauty and the one who frees from worldly existence.
They stared without a blink, not closing their eyes, while the Lord, palms joined, bowed his head.
uttar.33.cau3: Seeing their state, Śrī Rāma shed tears and the hair of his body stood on end.
The Lord took the great sages by the hand, sat them down and spoke words of the utmost charm:
uttar.33.cau4: Today I am blessed; listen, lords of sages: the sight of you wipes out sin.
The company of the good comes by great good fortune, and through it the round of birth is broken with no effort at all.
uttar.33.do33: The company of saints is the road to liberation, and the company of the sensual the road to worldly existence:
so say the saints, the poets, the learned, the Vedas, the Purāṇas and the good books.
uttar.34.cau1: Hearing the Lord's words, the four sages rejoiced and, thrilling all over, began a hymn of praise:
Glory to you, Lord, endless, free from every ill, sinless, many and one, full of compassion.
uttar.34.cau2: Glory to you who are beyond attributes, glory, glory to you, ocean of virtues, home of joy, beautiful and supremely refined.
Glory to you, consort of Lakṣmī; glory to you, upholder of the earth; peerless, unborn, without beginning, a mine of splendour.
uttar.34.cau3: You are a treasury of knowledge, free of pride yourself and giving honour to others; your holy fame is told by the Purāṇas and the Vedas.
You know the truth, you remember every kindness, you destroy ignorance; you have many names and yet no name, and are without stain.
uttar.34.cau4: You are all things, you pervade all and dwell for ever in every heart: protect us.
Shatter the pairs of opposites, our troubles and the snare of worldly existence; dwell in our hearts, Śrī Rāma, and crush desire and pride.
uttar.34.do34: Highest bliss, dwelling-place of compassion, you bring every wish of the heart to fulfilment.
Śrī Rāma, give us loving devotion that never fails.
uttar.35.cau1: Give us devotion, O Lord of the Raghus, the devotion that purifies above all and puts an end to the threefold affliction and the arrogance of worldly existence.
To those who bow before you, you are the wish-granting cow and the wish-fulfilling tree: be pleased, my Lord, and give us this boon.
uttar.35.cau2: O Lord of the Raghus, you are Agastya to the ocean of worldly existence; you are easily won by service and give every joy.
Rend the cruel sorrows born of the mind, friend of the lowly, and let evenness of mind spread wide.
uttar.35.cau3: You drive away hope, fear, envy and the rest, and you increase humility, discernment and dispassion.
Crest-jewel of kings, ornament of the earth, give us devotion, the boat that crosses the river of birth and death.
uttar.35.cau4: You are the swan who dwells for ever in the Mānasa lake of the sages' minds; Brahmā and Śiva worship your lotus feet.
You are the banner of Raghu's line, the guardian of the bounds the Vedas set, and the devourer of time, karma, nature and the guṇas.
uttar.35.cau5: You carry souls across and are yourself the boat, and you take away every fault; ornament of the three worlds, you are the Lord of Tulasīdāsa.
uttar.35.do35: Praising him again and again and bowing their heads in love,
Sanaka and his brothers went to the abode of Brahmā, having received the boon they wanted most.
uttar.36.cau1: Once Sanaka and the others had departed for the world of Brahmā, the brothers bowed their heads at Śrī Rāma's feet.
All of them were shy of asking the Lord, and all of them looked towards Hanumān.
uttar.36.cau2: They longed to hear words from the Lord's own lips, the hearing of which removes every error.
The Lord, who knows all hearts, understood everything and asked: Tell me, Hanumān, what is it?
uttar.36.cau3: Then Hanumān, with joined palms, said: Listen, Lord, compassionate to the lowly.
My Lord, Bharata wants to ask you something, but his mind hesitates to put the question.
uttar.36.cau4: Śrī Rāma said: You know my nature, Hanumān. Has Bharata ever been in any way apart from me?
Hearing this from the Lord, Bharata clasped his feet and said: Listen, my Lord, remover of the distress of those who bow to you.
uttar.36.do36: My Lord, I have no doubt at all, nor grief nor delusion even in a dream.
It is all your grace alone, you who are grace and bliss in fullness.
uttar.37.cau1: Treasury of mercy, I am going to make bold: I am your servant, and you give joy to your own.
O Lord of the Raghus, the Vedas and the Purāṇas have sung the glory of saints in many ways.
uttar.37.cau2: You too have praised them with your own lips, and the Lord's love for them is great.
My Lord, ocean of mercy, wise in virtues and knowledge, I wish to hear what marks them out.
uttar.37.cau3: Protector of those who bow to you, explain to me the difference between the saint and the wicked, setting each apart.
Śrī Rāma said: Listen, brother: the marks of saints are countless and well known in the Vedas and the Purāṇas.
uttar.37.cau4: Saints and the wicked behave towards each other as sandalwood and the axe do.
Listen, brother: the axe cuts down the sandal tree of Malaya, and the tree gives it its own virtue, filling it with fragrance.
uttar.37.do37: That is why sandalwood is placed on the heads of the gods and is loved by all the world,
while the axe's blade gets this penalty: it is burnt in the fire and pounded with the sledge.
uttar.38.cau1: Saints are not greedy for the things of the senses; they are mines of good conduct and virtue; they grieve at another's grief and rejoice at another's joy.
They are even-minded, have no enemy, are free of pride and dispassionate, and have given up greed, anger, elation and fear.
uttar.38.cau2: Their hearts are tender, they are kind to the lowly, and in thought, word and deed their devotion to me is without guile.
They honour everyone and seek no honour for themselves. Bharata, such beings are as dear to me as my own life.
uttar.38.cau3: They are free of desire and wholly given to my Name; they are homes of peace, dispassion, humility and gladness.
They have coolness, simplicity, friendliness and a love for the feet of brāhmaṇas, which gives birth to dharma.
uttar.38.cau4: Dear one, know the one in whose heart all these marks dwell to be a true saint, always.
Such people never waver from calm, self-restraint, their observances and right conduct, and never speak a harsh word.
uttar.38.do38: Those to whom blame and praise are alike, and whose attachment is to my lotus feet,
those good people, homes of virtue and stores of joy, are dear to me as my life.
uttar.39.cau1: Now hear the nature of the wicked: never keep their company, not even by mistake.
Their company always brings sorrow, as an unruly cow spoils a good kapilā cow.
uttar.39.cau2: The hearts of the wicked burn with a fierce heat; they are for ever burning at the sight of another's wealth.
Wherever they hear someone else run down, they are as delighted as if they had found a treasure just lying there.
uttar.39.cau3: They are given over to desire, anger, pride and greed; they are pitiless, deceitful, crooked, and homes of sin.
They bear enmity to everyone without cause, and do harm even to the one who does them good.
uttar.39.cau4: False is their taking and false their giving, false their meal and false their snack of parched grain.
They speak sweet words like the peacock, and are as hard of heart as the peacock, which devours great snakes.
uttar.39.do39: They harm others and are set on other men's wives, other people's wealth and the slander of others.
Such men are base and steeped in sin: man-eating demons in human form.
uttar.40.cau1: Greed is their blanket and greed their bed; they live for lust and the belly and have no fear of Yama's city.
If they hear anyone praised, they draw long breaths as though a fit of ague had come on them.
uttar.40.cau2: When they see anyone in trouble, they are as happy as if they had become kings of the world.
They are set on their own interest, at odds with their families, given over to lust and greed, and very wrathful.
uttar.40.cau3: They do not heed mother, father, teacher or brāhmaṇa; they go to ruin and destroy others as well.
In their delusion they bear ill will to others, and they have no taste for the company of saints or for the story of Śrī Hari.
uttar.40.cau4: They are oceans of faults, slow of wit and lustful; they mock the Vedas and lord it over others' wealth.
They bear ill will to others, and to brāhmaṇas most of all; they hide pretence and deceit in their hearts and put on a fine appearance.
uttar.40.do40: Such base and wicked people are not found in the Kṛta and Tretā ages;
in the Dvāpara there are a few, and in the Kali age there will be crowds of them.
uttar.41.cau1: Brother, there is no dharma like doing good to others, and nothing so low as causing others pain.
This is the settled finding of all the Purāṇas and the Vedas, dear one, as I tell it; the learned know it well.
uttar.41.cau2: Those who, having a human body, give pain to others suffer the heavy hardships of worldly existence.
Swayed by delusion, men commit many sins; bent on self-interest, they ruin their world to come.
uttar.41.cau3: To them, brother, I am death itself, the one who gives the fruit of good and evil deeds.
Knowing this, the truly wise, who have seen the sorrows of the round of births, worship me.
uttar.41.cau4: They leave behind all action that yields good or ill, and worship me, Lord of gods, men and sages.
I have told you the qualities of saints and of the wicked; those who have understood them and kept them in mind do not fall into worldly existence.
uttar.41.do41: Listen, dear one: merits and faults are many, and all of them are made by māyā.
The merit lies in seeing neither of them; to see them is itself a want of discernment.
uttar.42.cau1: Hearing these words from the Lord's own lips, all the brothers were overjoyed; their love was more than their hearts could hold.
Again and again they made humble entreaty to him, and Hanumān's heart was filled with boundless joy.
uttar.42.cau2: Then Śrī Rāma went to his own palace, and in this way he performed new acts every day.
Again and again the sage Nārada would come and sing the holy deeds of Śrī Rāma.
uttar.42.cau3: Having seen the ever-new deeds, the sage would go and tell the whole story in Brahmā's world.
Brahmā, hearing it, would be filled with delight and say: Dear one, sing his praises again and again.
uttar.42.cau4: Sanaka and his brothers praise Nārada; though these sages are devoted to Brahman,
on hearing the praises they forget their samādhi and listen with reverence, for they are the most worthy of hearers.
uttar.42.do42: Even those who are free while still in the body and absorbed in Brahman leave their meditation to hear these deeds;
those who take no delight in the story of Śrī Hari have hearts of stone.
uttar.43.cau1: Once Śrī Rāma sent for them, and the guru, the Brahmins and all the citizens came.
When the guru, the sages, the Brahmins and the good had taken their seats, the Lord, who ends worldly existence for his devotees, spoke these words:
uttar.43.cau2: Listen to my words, all you citizens. I do not say this out of any attachment in my heart.
There is no wrong in it, and no lording it over you. Listen, and do whatever pleases you.
uttar.43.cau3: Whoever accepts my command is my servant, and he is the one most dear to me.
Brothers, if I say anything that is not right, set fear aside and stop me.
uttar.43.cau4: It is by great good fortune that you have gained a human body, which all the scriptures declare to be rare even for the gods.
It is the home of spiritual practice and the door to liberation. One who gains it and still does not set right his next world
uttar.43.do43: suffers in the world beyond, and beats his head again and again in remorse,
laying false blame on Time, on karma and on God.
uttar.44.cau1: Brothers, sense pleasure is not the fruit of this body; even heaven is brief and brings sorrow in the end.
Those who gain a human body and give their minds to the objects of the senses are fools who take poison in exchange for nectar.
uttar.44.cau2: No one ever calls him wise who loses the philosopher's stone and picks up a guñjā seed.
This imperishable soul wanders through the four kinds of origin and the eighty-four lakh species.
uttar.44.cau3: It wanders on and on, pushed by māyā, caught in the ring of Time, karma, its own nature and the guṇas.
Now and then God, who loves without cause, has compassion and gives it a human body.
uttar.44.cau4: The human body is a boat for the ocean of worldly existence, and my grace the favourable wind;
the true guru is the helmsman of this sturdy boat. Thus means that are hard to come by have been made easy for it to gain.
uttar.44.do44: The man who has all this at hand and still does not cross the ocean of worldly existence
is ungrateful and dull of mind, and goes the way of one who destroys himself.
uttar.45.cau1: If you want happiness in the next world and here, hear my words and hold them firmly in your hearts.
Brothers, this path is easy and gives joy: devotion to me, which the Purāṇas and the Vedas have sung.
uttar.45.cau2: Knowledge is hard to reach, and many things stand in its way; its practice is hard, and the mind finds no prop in it.
Even if someone gains it after much hardship, without devotion he too is not dear to me.
uttar.45.cau3: Devotion depends on nothing else and is a mine of every joy, yet no creature gains it without the company of the good.
Without a store of merit one does not meet saints, and the company of the good puts an end to the round of births.
uttar.45.cau4: There is one act of merit in the world and no second: to worship the feet of the Brahmins in thought, deed and word.
Sages and gods look with favour on one who serves the Brahmins without deceit.
uttar.45.do45: With folded hands I tell you all one more secret teaching:
without worship of Śiva no one gains devotion to me.
uttar.46.cau1: Tell me, what labour is there on the path of devotion? It needs no yoga, no sacrifice, no japa, austerity or fasting;
only a simple nature, a mind without crookedness, and contentment always with whatever comes.
uttar.46.cau2: If one who calls himself my servant still puts his hope in men, tell me, what kind of faith is that?
Why say more and draw out the talk? Brothers, it is this conduct that wins me over.
uttar.46.cau3: He who has no enmity or strife, no hope and no fear, finds every quarter full of joy at all times.
One who starts no ventures out of desire, has no home of his own, is free of pride, sin and anger, and is capable and rich in realised knowledge,
uttar.46.cau4: who always loves the company of the good, to whom the objects of the senses, heaven and liberation are as straw,
who holds fast to the side of devotion yet without perversity, and has swept away all wicked argument,
uttar.46.do46: who delights in my many virtues and my name, and is rid of attachment, pride and delusion:
his joy is known only to one who is himself a mass of supreme bliss.
uttar.47.cau1: As soon as they heard Śrī Rāma's nectar-like words, all of them clasped the feet of the abode of mercy.
They said: O treasury of mercy, you are our mother, father, guru and brother, dearer to us than life.
uttar.47.cau2: Rāma, you are our body, our wealth, our home and our well-wisher; in every way you take away the pain of those who bow to you.
No one but you gives such counsel; even mother and father are bent on their own interest.
uttar.47.cau3: O foe of the demons, there are only two in the world who do good without a motive: you and your servants.
All others in the world are friends for their own ends; my Lord, not even in a dream do they seek the highest good.
uttar.47.cau4: Hearing everyone's words, steeped in the sweetness of love, Śrī Rāma rejoiced at heart.
Given leave, they went to their own homes, talking of the Lord's lovely words.
uttar.47.do47: Umā, the men and women of Ayodhyā are fulfilment itself,
for there Śrī Rāma, Brahman, dense with being, consciousness and bliss, is king.
uttar.48.cau1: Once the sage Vasiṣṭha came to where Śrī Rāma, the lovely abode of joy, was.
Śrī Rāma received him with great honour, washed his feet and took the water of the washing.
uttar.48.cau2: The sage said with folded hands: Listen, Rāma, ocean of mercy, to a request of mine.
Watching your conduct again and again, a boundless bewilderment rises in my heart.
uttar.48.cau3: Your glory is boundless, my Lord, and not even the Vedas know it; how am I to tell of it?
The office of family priest is a very low one; the Vedas, the Purāṇas and the smṛtis condemn it.
uttar.48.cau4: When I would not take it up, Brahmā said to me: Son, it will bring you gain hereafter.
Brahman, the Supreme Self, will take human form and be king, the ornament of the line of Raghu.
uttar.48.do48: Then I reflected in my heart: the one for whom yoga, sacrifice, vows and charity are performed
I shall gain through this very work; no other dharma equals it.
uttar.49.cau1: Japa, austerity, observances, yoga, one's own duty, the many good works that spring from the Vedas,
knowledge, compassion, self-restraint, bathing at holy places, every dharma that the Vedas and the good speak of,
uttar.49.cau2: and the reading and hearing of the many Āgamas, Vedas and Purāṇas have but one fruit, my Lord:
unbroken love for your lotus feet. This is the lovely fruit of every practice.
uttar.49.cau3: Is dirt washed away with dirt? Does anyone get ghee by churning water?
O Lord of the Raghus, without the water of loving devotion the dirt within never goes.
uttar.49.cau4: He alone knows all, he alone knows the truth and is learned; he is the home of virtues, with realised knowledge unbroken;
he is capable and has every good mark, who loves your lotus feet.
uttar.49.do49: My Lord, there is one boon I ask; Rāma, be gracious and grant it:
in birth after birth may my love for the Lord's lotus feet never lessen.
uttar.50.cau1: With these words the sage Vasiṣṭha came home; he had greatly pleased the heart of the ocean of mercy.
The Lord, giver of joy to his servants, took Hanumān and his brothers, Bharata and the rest, with him,
uttar.50.cau2: and the compassionate Lord went out of the city and had elephants, chariots and horses brought.
He looked at them all and graciously praised them, and gave them fittingly to whoever wanted them.
uttar.50.cau3: The Lord who takes away all weariness grew weary himself and went to a cool mango grove.
Bharata spread out his own cloth; the Lord sat down, and all the brothers attended on him.
uttar.50.cau4: Then the son of the Wind fanned him, his body thrilling and his eyes filling with tears.
There is no one as fortunate as Hanumān, nor anyone who loves Śrī Rāma's feet as he does.
uttar.50.cau5: Pārvatī, the Lord has praised his love and service again and again with his own lips.
uttar.50.do50: At that moment the sage Nārada came, his vīṇā in his hand,
and began to sing of the sweet glory of Śrī Rāma, which is ever new:
uttar.51.cau1: Look upon me, lotus-eyed Lord, whose gracious glance frees from sorrow.
Dark as a blue lotus, you are a bee drinking the nectar in the heart-lotus of Kāma's enemy, O Hari.
uttar.51.cau2: You break the might of the demon hosts, delight sages and the good, and destroy sin;
you are a mass of fresh clouds to the crop that is the Brahmins, refuge of those without refuge, and one who takes the lowly to himself.
uttar.51.cau3: You whose strong arms broke the earth's great burden, you skilled in slaying Khara, Dūṣaṇa and Virādha,
foe of Rāvaṇa, joy itself, best of kings, moon to the night-lotus of Daśaratha's line, glory to you!
uttar.51.cau4: Your fair fame is known in the Purāṇas, the Vedas and the Āgamas, and assemblies of gods, sages and saints sing it.
Compassionate, breaker of false pride, skilled in every way, you are the adornment of Kosala.
uttar.51.cau5: Your name churns away the filth of the Kali age and destroys attachment. Lord of Tulasīdāsa, protect the one who bows before you.
uttar.51.do51: Having lovingly told of Śrī Rāma's many virtues, the sage Nārada
held the ocean of beauty in his heart and went to Brahmā's realm.
uttar.52.cau1: Listen, Pārvatī: I have told this pure story in full, as far as my understanding goes.
Śrī Rāma's deeds are a thousand million and without end; neither the Vedas nor Sarasvatī can tell them to the end.
uttar.52.cau2: Śrī Rāma is endless, his virtues endless, and endless too his births, deeds and names.
The drops of water and the specks of dust on the earth might be counted, but the telling of Śrī Rāma's deeds never comes to an end.
uttar.52.cau3: This pure story gives the abode of Śrī Hari, and hearing it brings unfailing devotion.
Umā, I have told the whole lovely story that Kākabhuśuṇḍi told Garuḍa, king of birds.
uttar.52.cau4: I have described some of Śrī Rāma's virtues in detail. Now, Pārvatī, tell me what more I should say.
Hearing the blessed story, Umā was glad, and spoke in a very humble and gentle voice:
uttar.52.cau5: Blessed, blessed, blessed am I, foe of Tripura, for I have heard the virtues of Śrī Rāma that rid us of the fear of worldly existence.
uttar.52.do52क: Abode of mercy, by your grace I have now gained all I sought, and no delusion is left in me.
My Lord, I have come to know the glory of Śrī Rāma, the fullness of consciousness and bliss.
uttar.52.do52ख: My Lord, the moon of your face pours out the nectar of the story of Śrī Rāma;
O steady-minded one, my mind drinks it through the cups of my ears and is never sated.
uttar.53.cau1: Those who have had their fill of hearing Śrī Rāma's deeds have never known their special savour.
Even the great sages who are liberated while living go on hearing the virtues of Śrī Hari without end.
uttar.53.cau2: For one who wants to reach the far shore of the ocean of worldly existence, the story of Śrī Rāma is a sturdy boat.
And even for those given to the senses, the many virtues of Śrī Hari are a joy to the ears and a delight to the mind.
uttar.53.cau3: Who is there in the world with ears who does not love the deeds of Śrī Rāma?
Those who find no pleasure in the story of Śrī Rāma are dull creatures who destroy their own selves.
uttar.53.cau4: My Lord, you have sung this Mānasa of the deeds of Śrī Hari, and hearing it I have found boundless joy.
You said that this lovely story was sung by Kākabhuśuṇḍi to Garuḍa.
uttar.53.do53: He is firm in dispassion, knowledge and realised knowledge, and has deep love for Śrī Rāma's feet;
yet devotion to Śrī Rāma in the body of a crow: about this I have the gravest doubt.
uttar.54.cau1: Hear me, Purāri: of a thousand men, one may be found who keeps a vow of dharma.
Among ten million who live by dharma, someone turns away from the objects of sense and gives himself to dispassion.
uttar.54.cau2: The Veda says that among ten million of the dispassionate, scarcely one gains true knowledge.
Among ten million who have knowledge, scarcely one in the world is liberated while living.
uttar.54.cau3: Among a thousand of these, rare is the one of realised knowledge, absorbed in Brahman, a mine of every joy.
Of all beings, the righteous, the dispassionate, the knowing, the liberated while living and those absorbed in Brahman,
uttar.54.cau4: rarest of all, O lord of the gods, is one devoted to Śrī Rāma, rid of pride and māyā.
How did a crow come by such devotion to Śrī Hari? Lord of the universe, explain it to me.
uttar.54.do54: Wholly given to Śrī Rāma, intent on knowledge, a home of virtues, steady of mind:
tell me, my Lord, for what reason did he receive the body of a crow?
uttar.55.cau1: Compassionate one, tell me where the crow obtained this pure and lovely story of the Lord.
And how did you hear it, enemy of Kāma? Tell me, for I am very curious.
uttar.55.cau2: Garuḍa is greatly wise, a heap of virtues, a servant of Śrī Hari who lives very close to him.
Why did he pass over the hosts of sages and go to a crow to hear the story?
uttar.55.cau3: Tell me how the dialogue came about between these two devotees of Śrī Hari, the crow and Garuḍa, the eater of serpents.
Hearing Gaurī's simple, pleasing words, Śiva was glad and said with warm regard:
uttar.55.cau4: Blessed are you, Satī; your understanding is pure, and your love for Śrī Rāma's feet is no small thing.
Now hear a most holy history, on hearing which the delusion of the whole world is dispelled,
uttar.55.cau5: faith in Śrī Rāma's feet springs up, and a person crosses the ocean of worldly existence without effort.
uttar.55.do55: The king of birds too went to the crow and asked just such questions.
I shall tell you all of it with reverence; listen, Umā, with your whole mind.
uttar.56.cau1: Hear, fair-faced one with lovely eyes, how I came to hear this story that sets one free from worldly existence.
Your first descent was in Dakṣa's home, and in that birth you were called Satī.
uttar.56.cau2: When Dakṣa's sacrifice brought you insult, your anger was so great that you gave up your life.
My attendants laid the sacrifice in ruins; all that happened then you know well.
uttar.56.cau3: Then my mind was filled with sorrow, and I grieved at being parted from you, my beloved.
In a mood of detachment I roamed about, looking at the sights of lovely forests, mountains, rivers and lakes.
uttar.56.cau4: Far to the north of Mount Sumeru there is a blue mountain of great beauty.
Its golden peaks are lovely, and four fair ones among them won my heart.
uttar.56.cau5: On each of them stands a single huge tree: a banyan, a pīpal, a pākar and a mango.
Crowning the mountain is a lovely lake; one look at its steps of gems and the mind is charmed.
uttar.56.do56: The lake holds cool, pure, sweet water and a wealth of lotuses in many colours;
the swans in their flocks call with a soft, sweet cry, and lovely bees hum.
uttar.57.cau1: On that lovely mountain lives the bird; even at the end of an age of creation he does not perish.
The many merits and faults that māyā has made, delusion, desire and the rest of unwisdom,
uttar.57.cau2: which pervade the whole world, never come near that mountain.
How the crow lives there and worships Śrī Hari, hear now, Umā, with love.
uttar.57.cau3: Under the pīpal tree he sits in meditation; under the pākar he performs the sacrifice of japa.
In the mango's shade he worships in his mind; apart from the worship of Śrī Hari he has no other work.
uttar.57.cau4: Under the banyan he tells episodes of the story of Śrī Hari, and many birds come to listen.
He sings the wondrous deeds of Śrī Rāma in many ways, with love and reverence.
uttar.57.cau5: All the swans of pure mind that live for ever on that lake listen to him.
Going there, I saw this marvel, and a rare joy rose within me.
uttar.57.do57: Then I took the form of a swan and stayed there for a time,
and having heard the virtues of Śrī Rāma with reverence, I came back to Kailāsa.
uttar.58.cau1: Girijā, I have told you the whole account of the time I went to that bird.
Now hear the story of why Garuḍa, the banner of the race of birds, went to the crow.
uttar.58.cau2: When Śrī Rāma played at battle — a deed I am ashamed to think of —
and let himself be bound by Indrajit, the sage Nārada then sent Garuḍa.
uttar.58.cau3: Once the bonds were cut the serpent-eater went off, yet his heart was seized by a fierce despondency.
Again and again his mind went back to the Lord being bound, and the foe of serpents pondered:
uttar.58.cau4: Brahman, all-pervading, stainless, the lord of speech, the Supreme Lord beyond māyā and delusion:
I heard that he had taken birth in the world, yet I saw nothing of that power.
uttar.58.do58: He whose name men repeat to be freed from the bonds of worldly existence,
that same Rāma a petty demon has tied in a noose of serpents!
uttar.59.cau1: He reasoned with his mind in many ways, but knowledge did not dawn, and confusion clouded his heart.
Worn with distress, his mind piling up arguments, he fell under delusion just as you did.
uttar.59.cau2: Distraught, he sought out the divine sage and laid before him the doubt that troubled him.
Hearing it, Nārada was filled with pity and said: Listen, Garuḍa; the māyā of Śrī Rāma is mighty.
uttar.59.cau3: It steals away the minds even of the wise and by sheer force fills them with delusion.
It has made me dance many a time, king of birds, and it is this that now pervades you.
uttar.59.cau4: A great delusion has arisen in your heart, Garuḍa, and it will not soon go at my words.
King of birds, go to the four-faced Brahmā and do whatever he bids you.
uttar.59.do59: So saying, the divine sage went on his way, singing the virtues of Śrī Rāma,
and in his great wisdom he spoke again and again of the might of Śrī Hari's māyā.
uttar.60.cau1: Then the king of birds went to Brahmā and set his doubt before him.
Brahmā heard it and bowed low to Śrī Rāma; as the Lord's might dawned on him, love welled up in him beyond measure.
uttar.60.cau2: The Creator reflected in his mind: Poets, scholars and the wise are all in the grip of māyā.
The power of Śrī Hari's māyā has no bounds; many a time it has made me dance.
uttar.60.cau3: This world of moving and unmoving beings was made by me; small wonder if the king of birds is deluded.
Then Brahmā spoke in gracious words: Maheśa knows the greatness of Śrī Rāma.
uttar.60.cau4: Son of Vinatā, go to Śiva; do not ask anyone anywhere else, dear one.
There your doubt will be removed. As soon as he heard Brahmā's words, the bird set off.
uttar.60.do60: Then, in great anxiety, the king of birds came to me.
Umā, I was then setting out for Kubera's home, and you had stayed on Kailāsa.
uttar.61.cau1: He bowed his head at my feet with reverence and then told me his doubt.
Hearing his entreaty and gentle words, Bhavānī, I said to him with love:
uttar.61.cau2: Garuḍa, we have met on the road; how can I make it clear to you here?
All doubt is broken only when one keeps the company of the good for a long time
uttar.61.cau3: and hears there the lovely story of Śrī Hari that the sages have sung in many ways,
whose theme in the beginning, the middle and the end is the Lord, Śrī Rāma, the Blessed One.
uttar.61.cau4: There is a place, brother, where Śrī Hari's story is told daily; I send you there, so go and hear it.
Hearing it, you will be rid of every doubt, and a deep love for Śrī Rāma's feet will grow in you.
uttar.61.do61: Without the company of the good there is no story of Śrī Hari, and without it delusion does not flee;
and until delusion is gone there is no firm love for Śrī Rāma's feet.
uttar.62.cau1: Without love Śrī Rāma is not found, though one practise yoga, austerity, knowledge and dispassion.
In the north is a beautiful blue mountain; there lives the gentle Kākabhuśuṇḍi.
uttar.62.cau2: He is supremely skilled in the path of devotion to Śrī Rāma, wise, a house of virtues, and very ancient.
Without pause he tells the story of Śrī Rāma, and fine birds of every kind listen with reverence.
uttar.62.cau3: Hear there the countless virtues of Śrī Hari, and your grief that springs from delusion will be gone.
Once I had made it all clear, he went off glad at heart, after bowing his head at my feet.
uttar.62.cau4: That is why, Umā, I gave him no explanation: through Śrī Rāma's grace the hidden reason had become clear to me.
At some time he must have grown proud, and the treasury of mercy wishes to take that pride away.
uttar.62.cau5: And partly for this reason too I did not keep him with me: a bird understands only a bird's speech.
The Lord's māyā is mighty, Bhavānī; who is so wise that it cannot delude him?
uttar.62.do62क: He who is the crown of the wise and of devotees, the mount of the Lord of the three worlds:
even him māyā deluded, and yet base men are full of pride.
uttar.62.do62ख: When māyā deludes even Śiva and Brahmā, what is any other poor creature?
Knowing this in their hearts, the sages worship the Lord, the master of māyā.
uttar.63.cau1: Garuḍa went to where Kākabhuśuṇḍi lived, whose mind is never dulled and whose devotion to Śrī Hari is unbroken.
As he looked on the mountain he grew glad at heart, and all māyā, delusion and care left him.
uttar.63.cau2: He bathed in the pond and drank its water, then went beneath the banyan tree with a glad heart.
Many aged birds had gathered there to hear the delightful deeds of Śrī Rāma.
uttar.63.cau3: Kākabhuśuṇḍi wished to begin the story, and at that very time Garuḍa, lord of birds, came there.
Seeing the king of all birds coming, the crow and the whole gathering with him were filled with joy.
uttar.63.cau4: He showed the king of birds great honour, welcomed him and asked how he fared, and seated him on a fine seat.
Then, having worshipped him with love, the crow spoke these sweet words:
uttar.63.do63क: My lord, king of birds, seeing you I am blessed.
Give me your command and I will carry it out now. For what purpose have you come, my lord?
uttar.63.do63ख: Garuḍa said gently: You are always the very form of fulfilment,
you whose praises Śiva himself has sung with reverence from his own lips.
uttar.64.cau1: Listen, dear sir: all that I came for is done, now that I have seen you.
Seeing your hermitage, so supremely holy, I am rid of delusion, of doubt and of confusions of many kinds.
uttar.64.cau2: Now the story of Śrī Rāma, which is utterly holy, which always gives joy and destroys sorrow in heaps:
tell it to me with reverence, dear sir; again and again I entreat you, my lord.
uttar.64.cau3: Kākabhuśuṇḍi heard Garuḍa's humble words, artless, full of love, pleasing and wholly pure.
His heart was filled with great eagerness, and he began to tell the tale of Śrī Rāma's virtues.
uttar.64.cau4: First, Bhavānī, with deep love he described at length the lake of Śrī Rāma's deeds.
Then he told of Nārada's boundless delusion, and after that of Rāvaṇa's coming into the world.
uttar.64.cau5: Next he sang of the Lord's descent to earth, and then, with all his heart, told of his childhood.
uttar.64.do64: With great joy in his heart he told the childhood deeds in many ways;
then he told of the sage's coming, and of Śrī Rāma's marriage.
uttar.65.cau1: Then he told of the episode of Śrī Rāma's consecration, and how the king's word shattered the joy of the kingdom.
He told too of the citizens' grief at parting, and of the talk between Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa.
uttar.65.cau2: He told of the going to the forest, the boatman's love, the crossing of the Gaṅgā and the stay at Prayāga.
He described the Lord's meeting with Vālmīki, and how the Lord made his home at Citrakūṭa.
uttar.65.cau3: Then came the minister's return to the city, the king's death and Bharata's arrival, with a full account of his love.
He told how, after the king's last rites, Bharata took the citizens with him to the place where the Lord, the home of joy, was staying.
uttar.65.cau4: Then Śrī Rāma reasoned with him in many ways, and he came back to Ayodhyā with the sandals.
He went on to describe Bharata's way of life, the deed of Indra's son, and the Lord's meeting with Atri.
uttar.65.do65: He told of Virādha's slaying and of how Śarabhaṅga gave up his body.
Then he described Sutīkṣṇa's love, and the Lord's time in the holy company of Agastya.
uttar.66.cau1: The hallowing of the Daṇḍaka forest he told next, and then sang of the bond of friendship with the vulture.
Then the Lord made his dwelling at Pañcavaṭī and ended the dread of all the sages.
uttar.66.cau2: Next came the peerless teaching given to Lakṣmaṇa, and how Śūrpaṇakhā was disfigured.
After that he described the slaying of Khara and Dūṣaṇa, and how Rāvaṇa came to learn the whole secret.
uttar.66.cau3: The talk between Rāvaṇa and Mārīca, and how it went, he told in full.
Then came the carrying off of the illusory Sītā, and something of Śrī Rāma's grief in separation.
uttar.66.cau4: He told how the Lord performed the vulture's last rites, and how he slew Kabandha and gave Śabarī the blessed state.
Then he told how Śrī Rāma, voicing his grief of separation, went to the shore of the lake.
uttar.66.do66क: He told of the Lord's talk with Nārada and of the meeting with Hanumān, son of the Wind;
then of the friendship with Sugrīva and the ending of Vāli's life.
uttar.66.do66ख: He told how, after anointing Sugrīva king, the Lord lived on Mount Pravarṣaṇa.
Then came the description of the rains and of autumn, Śrī Rāma's anger and the monkey king's fear.
uttar.67.cau1: He told how the king of the monkeys dispatched his monkeys and they hurried off to all the quarters to search for Sītā;
how they went into the cavern, and how the monkeys then met Sampāti.
uttar.67.cau2: He told how Hanumān, son of the Wind, heard the whole story and leapt across the boundless ocean;
how he entered Laṅkā, and then how he gave Sītā courage.
uttar.67.cau3: He laid waste the grove, counselled Rāvaṇa, burnt the city and leapt back over the ocean.
All the monkeys came to where Śrī Rāma was and brought him word that Sītā was well.
uttar.67.cau4: Then Śrī Rāma went with the army and camped on the ocean shore;
he told how Vibhīṣaṇa came and met him, and the story of the subduing of the ocean.
uttar.67.do67क: He told how the monkey army built the bridge and crossed to the far side of the ocean,
and how Aṅgada, Vāli's son, finest of heroes, went as envoy.
uttar.67.do67ख: He described in many ways the fighting between demons and monkeys,
and the might and prowess of Kumbhakarṇa and Meghanāda, and their end.
uttar.68.cau1: He told of the many ways the hordes of demons died, and of the battle between Śrī Rāma and Rāvaṇa;
of Rāvaṇa's death, Mandodarī's grief, Vibhīṣaṇa's kingship and the gods freed from sorrow.
uttar.68.cau2: Then came Sītā's reunion with Śrī Rāma, and the gods praising him with joined palms.
Then the Lord, the home of grace, mounted the Puṣpaka with the monkeys and set out for Ayodhyā.
uttar.68.cau3: The crow sang all the bright deeds of how Śrī Rāma came back to his own city.
Then he told of Śrī Rāma's coronation, and in describing the city spoke of many points of royal policy.
uttar.68.cau4: Kākabhuśuṇḍi told the whole story at length, Bhavānī, just as I have told it to you.
Having heard all of Śrī Rāma's story, Garuḍa spoke, his heart overflowing with joy:
uttar.68.so68क: My doubt is gone; I have heard all the deeds of Śrī Rāma.
By your grace, O jewel among crows, love for Śrī Rāma's feet has come to me.
uttar.68.so68ख: When I saw the Lord bound in battle, a great delusion came over me:
Śrī Rāma is the very mass of consciousness and bliss; why then should he be distressed?
uttar.69.cau1: When I saw deeds so entirely like a man's, a heavy doubt arose in my heart.
That very error I now take as a kindness to me; it was a favour shown me by the treasury of mercy.
uttar.69.cau2: Only one who is sorely tormented by the sun's heat knows the comfort of a tree's shade.
Had I not been so deeply deluded, dear sir, how could I ever have met you?
uttar.69.cau3: And how could I have heard this lovely and most wondrous story of Śrī Hari, which you have sung in so many ways?
This is the teaching of the Vedas, the Āgamas and the Purāṇas, and the siddhas and sages declare it without doubt:
uttar.69.cau4: Pure saints are met only by the one on whom Śrī Rāma looks with grace.
By Śrī Rāma's grace I have seen you, and by your kindness every doubt has left me.
uttar.69.do69क: The crow heard the words of the king of birds, full of humility and love.
His body thrilled, his eyes filled with tears, and his heart rejoiced greatly.
uttar.69.do69ख: A listener of good sense, gentle nature and purity, who loves the story and serves Śrī Hari:
finding such a one, Umā, the good reveal even what is most secret.
uttar.70.cau1: Kākabhuśuṇḍi, whose love for the lord of birds was no small thing, spoke again:
In every respect, my lord, you are to be revered by me, for you enjoy the grace of Śrī Rāma.
uttar.70.cau2: You have no doubt, no delusion, no māyā; my lord, it is you who have been kind to me.
Śrī Rāma made delusion the excuse for sending you, king of birds, and so did me honour.
uttar.70.cau3: King of birds, you have told me of your delusion; there is nothing strange in that, my lord.
Nārada, Śiva, Brahmā, Sanaka and the others, foremost of sages who know the Self:
uttar.70.cau4: Whom among them has delusion not blinded? Who in the world has not been made to dance by desire?
Whom has craving not driven mad? Whose heart has anger not scorched?
uttar.70.do70क: The wise, the ascetic, the hero, the poet, the learned, the storehouse of virtues:
which of them in this world has greed not made a mockery of?
uttar.70.do70ख: Whom has the pride of wealth not twisted? Whom has power not made deaf?
Who is there whom the arrows of a doe-eyed woman's glance have not struck?
uttar.71.cau1: Who has not suffered the delirium that the guṇas (the qualities of nature) bring on? Pride and arrogance have let no one go entirely free.
Whom has the fever of youth not driven wild? Whose good name has attachment not ruined?
uttar.71.cau2: Whom has envy not stained? Whom has the wind of grief not shaken?
Whom has the serpent of anxiety not devoured? Who in the world has escaped the grip of māyā?
uttar.71.cau3: Desire is a woodworm and the body is timber; who is so steadfast that this worm has not got into him?
The three cravings, for sons, for wealth and for standing in the world: whose mind have they not sullied?
uttar.71.cau4: All this is the family of māyā, mighty and measureless; who can describe it to the end?
Śiva and four-faced Brahmā themselves fear her; how should other beings count for anything?
uttar.71.do71क: Throughout the world spreads the fierce army of māyā.
Desire and its kin are its generals; hypocrisy, deceit and sham piety are its warriors.
uttar.71.do71ख: That māyā is the handmaid of Śrī Rāma; once understood, she too is unreal.
Yet without Śrī Rāma's grace she does not let go; I say this, my lord, with my foot set firm.
uttar.72.cau1: The māyā that sets the whole world dancing, whose ways no one has been able to discern:
that same māyā, Garuḍa, at a mere play of the Lord's brows, dances like a dancing-girl, her whole retinue with her.
uttar.72.cau2: He is Śrī Rāma, the very substance of being, consciousness and bliss, unborn, realised knowledge itself, the abode of beauty and strength.
He pervades all and is all that is pervaded; he is undivided, endless, complete, the Lord whose power never fails.
uttar.72.cau3: He is beyond the guṇas, vast, beyond speech and the senses, all-seeing, without blemish, unconquered;
free of attachment, formless, free of delusion, eternal, stainless, a mass of bliss.
uttar.72.cau4: He is beyond Nature, the Lord who dwells in every heart, Brahman, desireless, stainless, imperishable.
There is no ground for delusion here; can darkness ever go before the sun?
uttar.72.do72क: For his devotees' sake the Lord, Śrī Rāma, took the body of a king,
and performed supremely sanctifying deeds, just like an ordinary man.
uttar.72.do72ख: As an actor puts on many guises and dances,
showing the feeling proper to each, yet does not himself become any of them,
uttar.73.cau1: Such, Garuḍa, is the play of Śrī Rāma: it bewilders the demons and gives joy to his people.
Those whose minds are soiled, who are slaves to the senses and full of lust, ascribe delusion to the Lord in this way, my master.
uttar.73.cau2: When someone's eyes become diseased, he says the moon is yellow.
When someone is confused about direction, Garuḍa, he says the sun has risen in the west.
uttar.73.cau3: One sitting in a boat sees the world moving, and in his delusion takes himself to be still.
Children spin round, the houses and the rest do not, yet they call one another liars.
uttar.73.cau4: Delusion said of Śrī Hari is just like this, Garuḍa; not even in a dream is there any room for ignorance in him.
But those who are in māyā's grip, dull of mind and luckless, with many kinds of veil over their hearts,
uttar.73.cau5: those fools, out of obstinacy, raise doubts and lay their own ignorance on Śrī Rāma.
uttar.73.do73क: Those given to desire, anger, pride and greed, clinging to the home, which is sorrow itself,
how can they know Śrī Rāma? The fools lie fallen in a well of darkness.
uttar.73.do73ख: The attributeless form is very easy to reach, but the form with attributes no one knows.
Hearing of his many deeds, some easy to grasp and some beyond grasping, the minds of sages are thrown into confusion.
uttar.74.cau1: Listen, Garuḍa: as far as my understanding goes I shall tell the lovely story of Śrī Rāma's lordship.
And how I myself fell into delusion, my lord, that whole story too I shall relate to you.
uttar.74.cau2: Dear one, you are a vessel of Śrī Rāma's grace; you love the virtues of Śrī Hari, and you give me joy.
So I hide nothing from you, and I sing of a supreme and charming secret.
uttar.74.cau3: Hear the innate nature of Śrī Rāma: he never lets pride remain in one who is his.
Pride is the root of the round of births; it brings pains of many kinds and every sorrow.
uttar.74.cau4: So the treasury of mercy takes it away, for his tender care for his servant is very great.
Just as, my lord, when a sore forms on a child's body, the mother has it lanced as if she were hard-hearted.
uttar.74.do74क: Though at first the child is hurt and cries, unable to bear it,
the mother, intent on ending the disease, does not count the child's pain.
uttar.74.do74ख: In the same way Śrī Rāma takes away his servant's pride for his good.
Tulasīdāsa, why do you not cast off error and worship such a Lord?
uttar.75.cau1: Listen with all your mind, Garuḍa, as I tell of Śrī Rāma's grace and my own folly.
Whenever Śrī Rāma takes a human body and plays out many sports for his devotees,
uttar.75.cau2: then I go to the city of Ayodhyā and rejoice to watch his childhood play.
I go and see the great festival of his birth, and, captivated, stay there for five years.
uttar.75.cau3: Śrī Rāma as a child is my chosen deity; his body holds the beauty of a thousand million Kāmadevas.
Gazing and gazing at my Lord's face, Garuḍa, I make my eyes fulfil their purpose.
uttar.75.cau4: Taking the form of a small crow, I stay with Śrī Hari and watch his childhood play in all its colours.
uttar.75.do75क: Wherever he roams as a child, I fly along with him;
and the leftovers that drop in the courtyard I gather up and eat.
uttar.75.do75ख: Once Śrī Rāma played out all his sports to the utmost.
As he recalled that play of the Lord, Kākabhuśuṇḍi's body thrilled with joy.
uttar.76.cau1: Kākabhuśuṇḍi said: Listen, Garuḍa; the story of Śrī Rāma gives joy to his servants.
The king's palace is beautiful in every way, inlaid with gold and jewels of many kinds.
uttar.76.cau2: The lovely courtyard where the four brothers play every day is beyond description.
Śrī Rāma moves about the courtyard at his childish games, a joy to his mother.
uttar.76.cau3: His soft body is dark like an emerald, and every limb holds the beauty of many Kāmadevas.
His feet, soft and red as a new lotus, have lovely toes, whose nails take away the moon's lustre.
uttar.76.cau4: On them are four charming marks, the thunderbolt and the rest, and lovely anklets that tinkle sweetly.
Round his waist a pretty girdle of bells, finely made of gold and gems, chimes sweetly and looks lovely.
uttar.76.do76: On the belly are three lovely lines, and the navel is beautiful and deep.
On his broad chest shine a child's ornaments and clothes of many kinds.
uttar.77.cau1: His rosy palms, nails and fingers are charming, and lovely ornaments adorn his long arms.
His shoulders are a lion cub's, his neck like a conch; his chin is lovely and his face the very limit of beauty.
uttar.77.cau2: His speech is a lisping babble, his lips are red, and he has two and two little teeth, bright and fine.
His cheeks are charming, his nose is lovely, and his smile, like the moon's rays, delights everyone.
uttar.77.cau3: His eyes, like blue lotuses, set one free from worldly existence; a tilak of gorocana shines on his forehead.
His brows are arched, his ears even and lovely, and his dark curling locks spread their beauty.
uttar.77.cau4: A fine yellow frock looks lovely on him; his gleeful cries and his glances delight me.
That treasure of beauty plays in the king's courtyard and dances as he gazes at his own reflection,
uttar.77.cau5: and plays with me in many ways, which I am deeply ashamed to describe.
When he runs crowing with delight to catch me, I fly off, and then he shows me a sweet cake.
uttar.77.do77क: When I come near, the Lord laughs; when I fly away, he cries.
When I go near to take hold of his feet, he looks back at me again and again as he runs away.
uttar.77.do77ख: When I saw him at play just as any ordinary child plays, delusion took hold of me:
what sort of acts is the Lord performing, he who is the very mass of consciousness and bliss?
uttar.78.cau1: The moment I let this much into my mind, Garuḍa, māyā, sent by Śrī Rāma, came over me.
Yet that māyā brought me no pain, nor did it bind me to the round of births as it does other beings.
uttar.78.cau2: My lord, there is another reason here; listen to it with care, mount of Hari.
Unbroken knowledge is Sītā's Lord alone; all beings, moving and unmoving, are in māyā's power.
uttar.78.cau3: If everyone's knowledge stayed ever the same, tell me, how could one speak of a difference between God and the soul?
The soul, full of pride, is subject to māyā; and māyā, the mine of the guṇas, is subject to God.
uttar.78.cau4: The soul is dependent, the Lord is his own master; souls are many, the Lord of Lakṣmī is one.
This difference is māyā's making and unreal, yet it will not go without Śrī Hari, though one try ten million means.
uttar.78.do78क: One who seeks liberation without worship of Śrī Rāma,
is a beast without tail or horns, even if he is a man of knowledge.
uttar.78.do78ख: Let the full moon rise in all its sixteen digits with the whole host of stars,
and let every mountain be set ablaze with forest fire: without the sun the night does not go.
uttar.79.cau1: In the same way, Garuḍa, without worship of Śrī Hari the suffering of living beings does not end.
Ignorance does not take hold of Śrī Hari's servant; knowledge, sent by the Lord, takes hold of him.
uttar.79.cau2: So the servant is never lost, best of birds; his devotion, in which he stays distinct from the Lord, grows.
Śrī Rāma saw me bewildered by error and smiled; hear that special play.
uttar.79.cau3: No one grasped the secret of that sport, not his younger brothers, not his mother or father.
Dark of body, with rosy hands and feet, he ran on hands and knees to catch me.
uttar.79.cau4: Then I fled, Garuḍa, and Śrī Rāma stretched out his arm to seize me.
However far I flew into the sky, there I saw Śrī Hari's arm beside me.
uttar.79.do79क: I went as far as Brahmā's world, and as I flew I looked behind me:
between Śrī Rāma's arm and me, dear one, there were only two finger-breadths.
uttar.79.do79ख: Piercing the seven coverings, as far as I had power to go,
there I went, and seeing the Lord's arm there, I was again thrown into distress.
uttar.80.cau1: When terror seized me I shut my eyes; looking again, I found I had come to Kosalapura.
Seeing me, Śrī Rāma smiled, and as he laughed I passed at once into his mouth.
uttar.80.cau2: Listen, Garuḍa: within his belly I saw universes in great multitudes.
There were many worlds, most wonderful, each more finely made than the last.
uttar.80.cau3: I saw Brahmās and Śivas by the million, and stars, suns and moons beyond counting,
guardians of the worlds, Yamas and Kālas beyond counting, mountains beyond counting and vast lands,
uttar.80.cau4: boundless oceans, rivers, lakes and forests, and creation spread out in many forms;
gods, sages, siddhas, nāgas, men and kinnaras, and beings of the four kinds, moving and unmoving.
uttar.80.do80क: What was never seen or heard of, what the mind itself cannot hold:
all that marvel I saw; how could it be described?
uttar.80.do80ख: In each universe I stayed a hundred years,
and in this way I roamed on, seeing many a cosmic egg.
uttar.81.cau1: Each world had its own Brahmā, and its own Viṣṇu, Śiva, Manu and guardians of the quarters.
Men, gandharvas, ghosts, vetālas, kinnaras, demons, beasts, birds and serpents were different there too.
uttar.81.cau2: There were hosts of gods and dānavas of many kinds as well; every living being there was of another sort.
Earth, rivers, oceans, lakes and many mountains: the whole of creation there was altogether different.
uttar.81.cau3: In every universe I saw a form of my own, and many kinds of incomparable things.
Each world had an Ayodhyā of its own, a different Sarayū, and different men and women.
uttar.81.cau4: Listen, dear one: Daśaratha, Kausalyā, and the brothers Bharata and the rest appeared in many different forms.
In every universe Śrī Rāma had come down as an incarnation, and I watched his boundless childhood play.
uttar.81.do81क: Garuḍa, I saw everything different from world to world, and exceedingly wonderful.
I roamed through countless worlds, but nowhere did I see the Lord Śrī Rāma any different.
uttar.81.do81ख: The same childhood, the same beauty, the same compassionate Śrī Rāma.
Driven by the wind of delusion, I went on from world to world, seeing this.
uttar.82.cau1: As I wandered through many universes, a hundred aeons seemed to pass.
Roaming on and on, I reached my own hermitage, and there again I spent some time.
uttar.82.cau2: When I heard that my Lord had been born in Ayodhyā, I rose and ran, brimming with love and full of joy.
I went and saw the great festival of his birth, just as I sang of it to you before.
uttar.82.cau3: In Śrī Rāma's belly I saw many worlds; they could only be seen, never described.
There, too, I saw Śrī Rāma once more, the all-knowing, the master of māyā, the compassionate Lord.
uttar.82.cau4: I pondered it again and again, but my mind was clogged with the mire of delusion.
All this I saw within two ghaṛīs (under an hour), and with a deep delusion in my mind I was bewildered.
uttar.82.do82क: Seeing me so distressed, the compassionate Śrī Rāma then laughed.
Listen, steady-minded one: as soon as he laughed, I found myself outside his mouth.
uttar.82.do82ख: Śrī Rāma began once more to play the same childish games with me.
I reasoned with my mind in countless ways, but it found no rest.
uttar.83.cau1: Seeing this play, and grasping that majesty, I forgot the state of my body.
I fell to the ground, unable to speak a word but this: Save me, save me, protector of those in distress!
uttar.83.cau2: The Lord saw me overcome with love, and then he held back the power of his māyā.
The Lord laid his lotus hand on my head, and he who is kind to the lowly took away all my sorrow.
uttar.83.cau3: Śrī Rāma freed me from delusion, he who gives joy to his servants and is a mass of grace.
Thinking over and over of the majesty I had seen before, I felt immense joy in my heart.
uttar.83.cau4: Seeing the Lord's tender love for his devotees, a special love welled up in my heart.
With tears in my eyes, thrilling all over, and with joined palms, I then prayed to him in many ways.
uttar.83.do83क: Hearing my words full of love, and seeing his own servant so humble,
the Lord, abode of Lakṣmī, spoke words that were gentle, deep and full of comfort:
uttar.83.do83ख: Kākabhuśuṇḍi, know that I am greatly pleased, and ask for a boon:
the siddhis such as aṇimā, other riches, liberation, the mine of all joys,
uttar.84.cau1: knowledge, discernment, dispassion, realised knowledge, and the many virtues in the world that even sages find hard to attain:
all this I will give you today, without a doubt; ask for whatever your heart desires.
uttar.84.cau2: Hearing the Lord's words, I was filled with still greater love, and I began to reason in my mind.
The Lord has truly offered to give every joy, but he has not spoken of giving his own devotion.
uttar.84.cau3: Without devotion, every virtue and every joy is like a spread of dishes without salt.
Of what use is joy without worship? Thinking this, Garuḍa, I said:
uttar.84.cau4: My Lord, if you are pleased and would give me a boon, and if you show me grace and love,
then, my master, I ask for the boon my heart longs for; you are generous, and you know what lies within the heart.
uttar.84.do84क: That unbroken, pure devotion to you which the Vedas and Purāṇas sing of,
which great yogīs and sages seek, and which only a rare one finds by the Lord's grace,
uttar.84.do84ख: O wish-granting tree of the devotees, friend of all who bow to you, ocean of mercy, home of joy,
O Rāma, my Lord, in your mercy give me that same devotion to you.
uttar.85.cau1: Saying evamastu (so be it), Śrī Rāma spoke words that gave the greatest joy:
Listen, crow: you are wise by nature; why would you not ask for such a boon?
uttar.85.cau2: You have asked for devotion, the mine of all joys; no one in the world is as fortunate as you.
Sages who burn their bodies in the fire of japa and yoga do not attain it with millions of efforts.
uttar.85.cau3: I am delighted to see your wisdom; your asking for devotion pleased me greatly.
Listen, bird: by my grace all good qualities will now dwell in your heart.
uttar.85.cau4: Devotion, knowledge, realised knowledge, dispassion, yoga, my deeds, their secrets and their divisions:
you will know the distinctions of them all, by my grace, without the toil of spiritual practice.
uttar.85.do85क: None of the delusions born of māyā will touch you now.
Know me to be Brahman, who has no beginning and no birth, who is free of the guṇas, and in whom all virtues are stored.
uttar.85.do85ख: Devotees are always dear to me. Listen, crow: bearing this in mind,
keep an unshakable love for my feet in body, speech and mind.
uttar.86.cau1: Now hear my words, supremely pure, true and easy to grasp, set forth by the Vedas and other scriptures.
I tell you my own settled truth: listen, hold it in your mind, and leaving all else, worship me.
uttar.86.cau2: The world springs from my māyā, and in it live beings of every kind, moving and unmoving.
All are dear to me, all are created by me; but humans please me more than all.
uttar.86.cau3: Among them, the twice-born; among the twice-born, those who hold the Vedas; among those, the ones who follow the dharma of the Vedas;
among them the dispassionate are dear to me, then the wise, and dearer still than the wise are those of realised knowledge.
uttar.86.cau4: Dearer to me than them is my own servant, whose refuge is in me alone, with no other hope.
I tell you the truth again and again: no one is as dear to me as my servant.
uttar.86.cau5: One without devotion, be he Brahmā himself, is only as dear to me as any other being.
But a creature with devotion, even the lowliest, is dear to me as life: this is my word.
uttar.86.do86: Tell me, to whom is a servant who is pure, good-natured and right-minded not dear?
The Vedas and Purāṇas state this rule; listen carefully, crow.
uttar.87.cau1: A father may have many sons, each of a different nature, temperament and conduct.
One is learned, one an ascetic, one a knower; one wealthy, one brave, one generous;
uttar.87.cau2: one knows everything, one is devoted to dharma; the father's love for all of them is the same.
But one son is devoted to his father in word, thought and deed, and knows no other duty even in a dream.
uttar.87.cau3: That son is as dear to his father as his own life, though he may be ignorant in every way.
In the same way, all beings, moving and unmoving, with the animals, gods, humans and asuras among them,
uttar.87.cau4: this whole universe is my making, and my mercy rests equally on all.
But whoever among them gives up pride and māyā and worships me in mind, speech and body,
uttar.87.do87क: be it a man, one who is neither man nor woman, a woman, or any being, moving or unmoving,
whoever worships me with their whole being, free of deceit, is supremely dear to me.
uttar.87.so87ख: I tell you the truth, bird: a pure servant is as dear to me as life.
Bearing this in mind, give up every other hope and reliance, and worship me.
uttar.88.cau1: Time will never have power over you; remember me and worship me without ceasing.
I could not have enough of hearing the Lord's nectar-like words; my body thrilled and my heart was overjoyed.
uttar.88.cau2: That joy only the mind and the ears know; the tongue cannot describe it.
The joy of the Lord's beauty the eyes know, but how could they tell it? They have no speech.
uttar.88.cau3: Having taught me in many ways and given me joy, the Lord began again the same childish play.
With tears in his eyes and a somewhat sulky face, he looked at his mother, as though very hungry.
uttar.88.cau4: Seeing it, the mother rose anxiously and ran to him, and with tender words held him to her breast.
Keeping him in her lap she gave him milk to drink, singing the charming deeds of Śrī Rāma.
uttar.88.so88क: The joy for which Śiva, the enemy of Tripura, auspicious and the giver of joy, took on an inauspicious guise
is the joy in which the men and women of Ayodhyā are ever immersed.
uttar.88.so88ख: Those who have once, even in a dream, tasted the merest trace of that joy,
good and wise souls, Garuḍa, count even the bliss of Brahman as nothing.
uttar.89.cau1: Then I stayed in Ayodhyā for some time and watched the Lord's delightful childhood play.
By Śrī Rāma's grace I received the boon of devotion, and bowing at the Lord's feet I came back to my own hermitage.
uttar.89.cau2: Māyā has had no hold on me ever since Śrī Rāma made me his own.
I have sung to you this whole secret story of how Śrī Hari's māyā made me dance.
uttar.89.cau3: Now, Garuḍa, I tell you what I have known myself: without worship of Śrī Hari, afflictions do not go.
Listen, king of birds: Śrī Rāma's greatness cannot be known without his grace.
uttar.89.cau4: Without knowing it there is no faith, and without faith there is no love.
Without love, Garuḍa, devotion never grows firm, just as water leaves no smoothness that stays.
uttar.89.so89क: Can there be knowledge without a guru? Can there be knowledge without dispassion?
The Vedas and Purāṇas proclaim it: can joy be found without devotion to Śrī Hari?
uttar.89.so89ख: Dear one, can anyone find rest without a natural contentment?
Try millions of means and wear yourself out to the point of death: will a boat ever move without water?
uttar.90.cau1: Without contentment desires do not perish, and while desire remains there is no happiness, not even in a dream.
Can desires be ended without the worship of Śrī Rāma? Does a tree ever grow where there is no ground?
uttar.90.cau2: Does evenness of mind come without realised knowledge? Can anyone find room without the sky?
Without faith there is no dharma; can anyone find scent without the earth?
uttar.90.cau3: Does splendour spread without austerity? Without water, could the world have any taste?
Is good conduct found without serving the wise? No more, master, than there is form without light.
uttar.90.cau4: Does the mind grow steady without the joy of the self? Can there be touch without air?
Is any accomplishment won without faith? Just so, without the worship of Śrī Hari the fear of worldly existence does not end.
uttar.90.do90क: Without faith there is no devotion, and without devotion Śrī Rāma's heart does not melt.
Without Śrī Rāma's grace a living being finds no rest, not even in a dream.
uttar.90.so90ख: Considering this, O steady of mind, cast off all sophistry and doubt,
and worship Śrī Rāma, a mine of compassion, beautiful, the giver of joy.
uttar.91.cau1: My lord Garuḍa, I have sung the majesty and glory of the Lord as far as my understanding goes.
I have said nothing by way of any special contrivance; all this I have seen with my own eyes.
uttar.91.cau2: Glory, name, form and the tale of virtues: all are boundless, and Śrī Rāma himself is without end.
The sages sing Śrī Hari's virtues each as far as his mind reaches; the Vedas, Śeṣa and Śiva do not find their end.
uttar.91.cau3: Every winged creature, from you down to the mosquito, flies through the sky, yet none reaches its end.
So too, dear one, the glory of Śrī Rāma is fathomless: has anyone ever touched its bottom?
uttar.91.cau4: Śrī Rāma's body is as lovely as a thousand million Kāmadevas; like countless millions of Durgās he crushes his foes.
His pomp and pleasure equal those of a thousand million Indras; his expanse is boundless as a thousand million skies.
uttar.91.do91क: He has the vast strength of a thousand million winds and the light of a thousand million suns.
He is cool as a thousand million moons, and he stills every terror of worldly existence.
uttar.91.do91ख: Like a thousand million Deaths he is exceedingly hard to overcome, hard to approach, without end.
Like a thousand million comets the Lord is not to be withstood.
uttar.92.cau1: The Lord is fathomless as a thousand million nether worlds, and fearsome as a thousand million Yamas.
He purifies like countless millions of holy places; his name destroys the whole heap of sins.
uttar.92.cau2: Śrī Rāma is unshakeable as ten million Himālayas and deep as a thousand million oceans.
Like a thousand million wish-fulfilling cows, the Lord grants every desire.
uttar.92.cau3: His skill is that of countless millions of Sarasvatīs, his craft in creation that of a thousand million Brahmās.
He sustains like ten million Viṣṇus and destroys like a thousand million Rudras.
uttar.92.cau4: He is wealthy as a thousand million Kuberas, and like ten million Māyās a storehouse of the world's display.
In bearing the load he is like a thousand million Śeṣas; the Lord of the world is limitless and beyond compare.
uttar.92.cha1: He is beyond compare; there is no other to liken him to; Śrī Rāma is like Śrī Rāma alone, the Vedas say.
Just as the sun, when called the equal of a thousand million fireflies, is only made very small,
so the great sages extol Śrī Hari each by the play of his own mind;
and the Lord, who values the feeling and is most merciful, hears it with love and is pleased.
uttar.92.do92क: Śrī Rāma is an ocean of boundless virtues; can anyone find its bottom?
What I heard from the saints, just as I heard it, I have told you.
uttar.92.so92ख: The Lord is won by heartfelt feeling; he is a treasury of joy, a home of compassion.
Casting off attachment, pride and self-regard, one should always worship the beloved of Sītā.
uttar.93.cau1: Hearing Kākabhuśuṇḍi's lovely words, Garuḍa rejoiced and fluffed out his wings.
Tears filled his eyes, his heart was overjoyed, and he took Śrī Rāma's majesty into his heart.
uttar.93.cau2: Understanding his earlier delusion, he repented that he had taken the beginningless Brahman for a man.
Over and over he laid his head at the feet of the crow, whom he now knew to be like Śrī Rāma, and his love for him grew.
uttar.93.cau3: Without a guru no one crosses the ocean of worldly existence, not even one as great as Brahmā and Śiva.
Garuḍa said: Dear one, the snake of doubt had bitten me, and waves of sophistry rose upon me in painful throngs.
uttar.93.cau4: Śrī Rāma, giver of joy to his own, became the snake-charmer in your form and brought me back to life.
By your grace my delusion has perished, and I have come to know the peerless secret of Śrī Rāma.
uttar.93.do93क: Having praised him in many ways, bowing his head with folded hands,
Garuḍa spoke again in humble, loving and gentle words:
uttar.93.do93ख: My lord and master, it is from my own want of discernment that I ask you.
Ocean of mercy, think of me as your own servant and tell me with kindly care.
uttar.94.cau1: You know all things and know the truth; you are beyond darkness, wise, gentle and simple in conduct.
You are the dwelling of knowledge, dispassion and realised knowledge, and a dear servant of Śrī Rāma.
uttar.94.cau2: For what reason did you receive this body? Dear one, explain it all to me.
Master, you who range the sky, tell me where you found this lovely lake of Śrī Rāma's deeds.
uttar.94.cau3: My lord, I heard from Śiva that even in the great dissolution you do not perish.
Śiva, the Lord, never speaks idle words; and this too is a doubt in my mind.
uttar.94.cau4: Beings moving and unmoving, nāgas, men and gods: my lord, the whole world is a morning meal for Kāla, Time.
Kāla, who dissolves countless universes, is always mighty, and no one can pass beyond him.
uttar.94.so94क: What is the reason that Kāla, so very terrible, has no hold on you?
Tell me that, compassionate one: is it the power of knowledge or the strength of yoga?
uttar.94.do94ख: My lord, the moment I came to your hermitage my delusion and error fled.
What is the reason for that, my lord? Tell me all of it with love.
uttar.95.cau1: Umā, hearing Garuḍa's words Kākabhuśuṇḍi rejoiced and spoke with the deepest love:
Blessed, blessed is your understanding, Garuḍa. Your question is very dear to me.
uttar.95.cau2: Hearing your loving, lovely question, the memory of many births has come back to me.
I will tell you my whole story in song; dear one, listen with reverence and with your mind on it.
uttar.95.cau3: Repetition of the Name, austerity, sacrifice, calm of mind, restraint of the senses, vows, gifts, dispassion, discernment, yoga and realised knowledge:
the fruit of them all is love for the feet of Śrī Rāma, and without it no one finds well-being.
uttar.95.cau4: In this very body I gained devotion to Śrī Rāma, and so I feel great attachment to it.
Everyone feels attachment for that which serves some purpose of his own.
uttar.95.so95क: Garuḍa, this is a rule of conduct approved by the Veda, and the good say it too:
love even the very lowly when you know them to be for your highest good.
uttar.95.so95ख: Silk comes from a worm, and from silk comes beautiful silken cloth;
so everyone tends that worm as dearly as life, though it is utterly impure.
uttar.96.cau1: This is the true self-interest of a living being: love for Śrī Rāma's feet in thought, deed and word.
Holy and fair is that body alone which, once received, is spent in the worship of Śrī Rāma.
uttar.96.cau2: One turned away from Śrī Rāma may gain a body like Brahmā's, yet poets and the learned do not praise him.
In this body devotion to Śrī Rāma sprang up in my heart; therefore, master, it is supremely dear to me.
uttar.96.cau3: I do not leave this body, though my death is at my own will, for the Vedas tell of no worship without a body.
Delusion first brought me to great ruin; turned away from Śrī Rāma, I never once slept in peace.
uttar.96.cau4: Through many births I did many kinds of works besides: yoga, repetition of the Name, austerity, sacrifice and gifts.
What womb is there in which I was not born, Garuḍa, as I wandered and wandered through the world?
uttar.96.cau5: Master, I tried every kind of work and saw what came of it, but I was never as happy as I am now.
My lord, I remember many births; by Śiva's grace delusion did not close round my mind.
uttar.96.do96क: Now I will tell the story of my first birth; listen, Garuḍa.
Hearing it, love for the Lord's feet springs up, and by that every affliction is ended.
uttar.96.do96ख: My lord, in a former kalpa there was an age, the Kali age, the root of all impurity.
Men and women alike were bent on unrighteousness, and all of them went against the Veda.
uttar.97.cau1: In that Kali age I went to the city of Kosala and was born there, taking the body of a śūdra.
I served Śiva in thought, deed and word, reviled the other gods, and was proud.
uttar.97.cau2: Drunk with the pride of wealth, I was a great talker, harsh of mind, with vast hypocrisy in my heart.
Though I lived in the capital of Śrī Rāma, I knew nothing then of its glory.
uttar.97.cau3: Now I know the power of Avadh. The Vedas, the Āgamas and the Purāṇas sing that
whoever lives in Avadh, in any birth, is bound to become devoted to Śrī Rāma.
uttar.97.cau4: A living being knows the power of Avadh only when Śrī Rāma, bow in hand, dwells in his heart.
That Kali age was a hard one, Garuḍa; all men and women were given over to sin.
uttar.97.do97क: The impurity of Kali had swallowed every dharma, and the true scriptures had vanished.
Hypocrites, inventing out of their own minds, had brought forth many sects.
uttar.97.do97ख: All the people had fallen under delusion, and greed had swallowed good works.
Listen, mount of Hari, treasury of knowledge: I will tell you a little of the ways of the Kali age.
