uttar.98.cau1: The dharma of the varṇas is gone, and so are the four stages of life; all men and women are bent on opposing the Vedas.
Brahmins sell the Vedas, kings devour their subjects, and no one heeds the command of the Vedas.
uttar.98.cau2: The path is whatever pleases each one; the learned man is he who brags.
Whoever is given to false show and hypocrisy is called a saint by all.
uttar.98.cau3: The clever man is he who seizes another's wealth; the one who practises hypocrisy is the great observer of right conduct.
Whoever tells lies and knows how to jest is praised as gifted in the Kali age.
uttar.98.cau4: One who has no right conduct and has left the path of the Vedas is, in the Kali age, both the wise man and the man of dispassion.
The famous ascetic of the Kali age is the one whose nails and matted locks have grown long.
uttar.98.do98क: Those who wear inauspicious garb and ornaments and eat whatever is fit or unfit to be eaten,
they are the yogis, they the siddhas, they the people worshipped in the Kali age.
uttar.98.so98ख: Those whose conduct does harm are the ones held in esteem and honoured;
those who are false in thought, deed and word are the speakers of the Kali age.
uttar.99.cau1: My lord, all men are in the power of women and dance like a juggler's monkey.
Śūdras teach knowledge to Brahmins and, putting on the sacred thread, accept improper gifts.
uttar.99.cau2: All men are given to desire and greed and are quick to anger; they are hostile to the gods, Brahmins, the Vedas and the saints.
Ill-fated women leave a handsome husband who is a home of virtues and court another man.
uttar.99.cau3: Wives whose husbands live go without ornaments, while widows adorn themselves anew.
Guru and disciple are like the deaf and the blind: one does not hear, the other does not see.
uttar.99.cau4: The guru who takes his disciple's wealth but does not take away his grief falls into a terrible hell.
Mothers and fathers summon their children and teach them whatever dharma will fill the stomach.
uttar.99.do99क: Women and men talk of nothing but the knowledge of Brahman,
and these same people, ruled by greed, kill a Brahmin or a guru for a cowrie's worth.
uttar.99.do99ख: Śūdras argue with Brahmins: Are we in any way less than you?
He who knows Brahman is the best of Brahmins. And they glare at them and rebuke them.
uttar.100.cau1: Those who lust after other men's wives, are clever at deceit and are wrapped in delusion, malice and possessiveness,
these are the wise men who preach non-duality: such were the ways of the Kali age that I saw.
uttar.100.cau2: They are lost themselves, and they bring ruin on those too who anywhere keep to the true path.
Those who find fault with the Vedas by argument lie in one hell after another, each for a whole kalpa (aeon).
uttar.100.cau3: Those counted lowest among the varṇas, such as oil-pressers, potters, śvapacas (outcastes), Kirātas, Kols and liquor-sellers,
when a wife dies or the household's wealth is lost, shave their heads and become sannyāsīs.
uttar.100.cau4: They have Brahmins worship them, and with their own hands they ruin both worlds.
Brahmins are unlettered, greedy and lustful, without right conduct, foolish, and husbands of low-born women.
uttar.100.cau5: Śūdras perform japa, austerities and vows of many kinds, and sit on the seat of honour to recite the Purāṇas.
All people follow ways of their own invention; the boundless wrong cannot be described.
uttar.100.do100क: In the Kali age the varṇas became mixed, and all people broke through the bounds.
They commit sins and reap sorrow, fear, sickness, grief and separation.
uttar.100.do100ख: The path of devotion to Śrī Hari, approved by the Vedas and joined with dispassion and discernment,
men, in their delusion, do not walk in it, and invent many paths of their own.
uttar.101.cha1: Ascetics spend great sums to adorn their houses; sense-pleasures have stolen their dispassion and none is left.
The austere are rich and householders poor; dear one, the wonders of the Kali age cannot be told.
uttar.101.cau2: Men turn out a faithful wife of good family and, casting aside propriety, bring a maidservant into the house.
Sons honour mother and father only until they have looked on a wife's face.
uttar.101.cau3: From the time the in-laws' house grew dear, their own family became like enemies.
Kings are given to sin and have no dharma; they constantly torment their subjects with punishments.
uttar.101.cau4: The rich, though base, count as well-born; the mark of a Brahmin is his sacred thread, of an ascetic his bare body.
He who respects neither the Purāṇas nor the Vedas is, in the Kali age, the true servant of Śrī Hari and saint.
uttar.101.cau5: Poets come in throngs, but no generous patron is heard of in the world; fault-finders of merit are many, but not one person of merit.
In the Kali age famine falls again and again, and without food all people die in misery.
uttar.101.do101क: Listen, Garuḍa: in the Kali age deceit, obstinacy, hypocrisy, hatred, false creeds,
vanity, delusion, desire and the rest, and arrogance have spread over the whole universe.
uttar.101.do101ख: Men practise their dharma of japa, austerity, vows, sacrifice and charity in a spirit of darkness (tamas).
The gods send no rain on the earth, and the rice that is sown does not sprout.
uttar.102.cha1: Women, weak and helpless, have only their hair for ornament, and great hunger; they are poor and sorrowful, with attachments of many kinds.
Foolish, they want happiness but have no love for dharma; their minds are small and hard, with no gentleness.
uttar.102.cau2: Men are afflicted with disease and find enjoyment nowhere; they are proud and quarrel without cause.
Life is short, five or ten years, yet their vanity is as if they would not perish even at the end of the aeon.
uttar.102.cau3: The Kali age has brought men to ruin; no one respects even a younger sister or a daughter.
There is no contentment, no reflection, no calm; people of every caste, high or low, have become beggars.
uttar.102.cau4: Envy, harsh words and greed fill everything to the brim; evenness of mind is gone.
All people are struck down by separation and deep grief; the dharma and conduct of varṇa and āśrama have vanished.
uttar.102.cau5: Self-restraint, charity, compassion and good sense are gone; dullness and the cheating of others abound.
Women and men alike care only to feed the body; slanderers of others are spread across the world.
uttar.102.do102क: Listen, Garuḍa: the Kali age is a home of sins and vices;
yet the Kali age has great merit too: in it deliverance comes without effort.
uttar.102.do102ख: In the Kṛta, Tretā and Dvāpara ages there are worship, sacrifice and yoga;
the state these win, people reach in the Kali age by the name of Śrī Hari.
uttar.103.cau1: In the Kṛta age all are yogis and men of realised knowledge; by meditating on Śrī Hari, beings cross worldly existence.
In the Tretā age people perform sacrifices of many kinds and, offering their actions to the Lord, get across worldly existence.
uttar.103.cau2: In the Dvāpara age, worshipping the feet of Śrī Rāma, men cross worldly existence; there is no other way.
In the Kali age, simply by singing the tale of Śrī Hari's virtues, men find a footing in the ocean of existence.
uttar.103.cau3: In the Kali age there is no yoga, no sacrifice, no knowledge; the one support is singing Śrī Rāma's virtues.
Whoever gives up every other reliance, worships Śrī Rāma and sings his host of virtues with love,
uttar.103.cau4: he and no other crosses worldly existence, without any doubt; the power of the Name is plain to see in the Kali age.
The Kali age has one holy power: merit in the mind bears fruit, but sin in the mind does not count.
uttar.103.do103क: If one has faith, there is no age like the Kali age;
singing the spotless host of Śrī Rāma's virtues, one crosses worldly existence without effort.
uttar.103.do103ख: Dharma plainly has four feet, and in the Kali age one of them is chief;
that is giving: a gift, made by any means at all, does good.
uttar.104.cau1: Moved by Śrī Rāma's māyā, the dharmas of all the ages arise in every heart day after day.
Pure sattva, evenness, realised knowledge and a cheerful mind: know these as the working of the Kṛta age.
uttar.104.cau2: Much sattva, a little rajas, a love of action and happiness of every kind: this is the dharma of the Tretā age.
Much rajas, very little sattva, some tamas, and joy and fear in the mind: this is the dharma of the Dvāpara age.
uttar.104.cau3: Much tamas, little rajas and strife on every side: this is the working of the Kali age.
The wise, understanding in their minds the dharma of the ages, give up unrighteousness and love dharma.
uttar.104.cau4: The ways of the age do not touch one whose love for the feet of Śrī Rāma is great.
King of the birds, the trickery a juggler works is hard to see through, but the juggler's own servant is not taken in by that illusion.
uttar.104.do104क: The faults and merits wrought by Śrī Hari's māyā do not go without worship of Śrī Hari;
considering this in the mind, one should give up all desires and worship Śrī Rāma.
uttar.104.do104ख: Lord of birds, in that Kali age I lived many years in Ayodhyā;
then famine came, and driven by hardship I went to a foreign land.
uttar.105.cau1: Listen, Garuḍa: I went to Ujjain, wretched, dejected, poor and unhappy.
After some time I came by a little wealth, and there I took to the service of Śiva.
uttar.105.cau2: There was a Vedic Brahmin who always worshipped Śiva and had no other work.
He was a true saint and knew the highest truth; a worshipper of Śiva, he never reviled Śrī Hari.
uttar.105.cau3: I served him with deceit in my heart; the Brahmin was most kind and a home of right conduct.
My lord, the Brahmin saw how humble I seemed outwardly and taught me like a son.
uttar.105.cau4: The noble Brahmin gave me Śiva's mantra and taught me what was good in many ways.
I would go to Śiva's temple and repeat the mantra, while hypocrisy and egoism grew great in my heart.
uttar.105.do105क: I was wicked, my mind full of filth, of low birth and in the grip of delusion;
at the sight of Śrī Hari's devotees and Brahmins I burned, and I bore enmity to Viṣṇu.
uttar.105.so105ख: My guru counselled me daily, pained at what he saw of my conduct;
but great anger arose in me: does right counsel ever please a hypocrite?
uttar.106.cau1: Once my guru called me and taught me right conduct in many ways.
He said: Son, the fruit of serving Śiva is just this: unbroken devotion to Śrī Rāma's feet.
uttar.106.cau2: Dear one, Śiva and Brahmā themselves worship Śrī Rāma; what need, then, to speak of a lowly man?
Unlucky one, you hope to find happiness by hostility to him whose feet Brahmā and Śiva love?
uttar.106.cau3: My guru called Hara a servant of Hari, and hearing it, Garuḍa, my heart burned.
I was of low birth, and on gaining learning I became like a snake that has been fed milk.
uttar.106.cau4: Proud, crooked, ill-starred and low-born, I bore ill will to my guru day and night.
He was most compassionate, without the least anger, and again and again he gave me good counsel.
uttar.106.cau5: A base man strikes down and ruins first of all the very one through whom he gained his greatness.
Listen, brother: smoke, born of fire, rises to the rank of a cloud and puts that fire out.
uttar.106.cau6: Dust lies scorned on the road and bears the kicks of everyone, every day.
But when the wind lifts it, it first fills the wind itself, and then settles in the eyes of kings and on their crowns.
uttar.106.cau7: Listen, Garuḍa: understanding this, the wise keep no company with the base.
Poets and the learned sing this rule of conduct: with the wicked, neither quarrel nor friendship is good.
uttar.106.cau8: My master, one should always stay aloof, and shun the wicked as one would a dog.
I was wicked, with deceit and crookedness in my heart; my guru spoke for my good, but it did not please me.
uttar.106.do106क: Once I was in Śiva's temple, repeating the name of Śiva.
My guru came in, and in my pride I did not rise and bow to him.
uttar.106.do106ख: Compassionate as he was, he said nothing, and there was not a trace of anger in his heart.
But Maheśa could not bear the grave sin of slighting the guru.
uttar.107.cau1: A voice from the sky sounded in the temple: Wretch, ignorant and proud!
Though your guru feels no anger, being most merciful and of perfect understanding,
uttar.107.cau2: still, fool, I shall curse you, for I cannot abide a breach of right conduct.
Wicked one, if I do not punish you, my path of the Veda will be broken.
uttar.107.cau3: Fools who envy their guru lie in the Raurava hell for ten million ages.
Then they take bodies among the lower creatures and suffer pain for ten thousand births.
uttar.107.cau4: Sinner, you sat on like a python; wicked one, your mind steeped in filth, become a snake.
Go into the hollow of some great tree and stay there, lowest of the low, sunk to this base state.
uttar.107.do107क: Hearing Śiva's dreadful curse, my guru cried out in dismay.
Seeing me tremble violently, he felt anguish rise in his heart.
uttar.107.do107ख: The Brahmin prostrated himself with love and, facing Śiva, joined his palms.
Then, thinking of the terrible fate that awaited me, he began to pray in a voice choked with feeling.
uttar.108.cau1: O Īśāna, I bow to the Lord whose form is liberation, the mighty, the all-pervading, Brahman, the Veda itself.
Abiding in his own being, beyond attributes and all distinctions, free of desire, the sky of consciousness, dwelling in the sky: you I worship.
uttar.108.cau2: Formless, the root of Oṃ, the fourth state beyond the three, beyond speech, knowledge and the senses, the Lord, lord of the mountain,
terrible, the death even of Mahākāla, compassionate, the home of virtues, beyond the world: to him I bow.
uttar.108.cau3: Fair as the snowy mountain and deep, his body bright with the radiance and beauty of ten million Kāmas;
on his head the lovely Gaṅgā shimmers in waves, the young moon gleams on his brow, and serpents lie at his throat;
uttar.108.cau4: his earrings swaying, his brows fair and his eyes large and lovely, his face serene, his throat blue, full of compassion;
clad in the skin of the lion, garlanded with skulls: Śaṅkara, the beloved, the Lord of all, I worship.
uttar.108.cau5: The fierce, the supreme, the bold, the highest Lord, the undivided, the unborn, shining like ten million suns,
who uproots the three kinds of pain, trident in hand, reached through loving feeling: the lord of Bhavānī I worship.
uttar.108.cau6: You who are beyond all parts, the auspicious, who bring the aeon to its end, ever the giver of joy to the good, enemy of Tripura,
mass of consciousness and bliss, dispeller of delusion, enemy of Kāma: my Lord, be gracious, be gracious.
uttar.108.cau7: Lord of Umā, as long as men, in this world or the next, do not worship your lotus feet,
they find no happiness, no peace, no end to their torment. Be gracious, my Lord, who dwell in all beings.
uttar.108.cau8: I know neither yoga nor japa nor worship; Śambhu, at every moment and always, I bow to you.
My Lord, I am scorched by the flood of the sorrows of age and birth and have fallen into distress: protect me, O Īśa, O Śambhu.
uttar.108.shloka9: This Rudrāṣṭaka was spoken by the Brahmin to please Hara.
Śiva is gracious to those who recite it with devotion.
uttar.108.do108क: Śiva, who knows all, heard the prayer and saw the Brahmin's love.
Then again a voice from the sky sounded in the temple: Best of Brahmins, ask for a boon.
uttar.108.do108ख: The Brahmin said: Lord, if you are pleased with me, and, master, if you love the lowly,
then, Lord, grant me first devotion to your own feet, and after that a second boon.
uttar.108.do108ग: The soul is dull; in the power of your māyā it wanders, always astray.
Lord, ocean of mercy, Bhagavān, do not be angry with it.
uttar.108.do108घ: Śiva, kind to the lowly, be merciful to him now,
so that, my Lord, before long the curse may give way to grace.
uttar.109.cau1: Treasury of mercy, now do that which will bring him the highest good.
Hearing the Brahmin's words, steeped in the good of another, the voice from the sky said: So be it.
uttar.109.cau2: Though he has committed a dreadful sin, and I in my anger have cursed him,
yet, seeing your goodness, I shall show him special grace.
uttar.109.cau3: Brahmins who are forgiving and do good to others are as dear to me as Śrī Rāma, slayer of Khara.
Brahmin, my curse will not go for nothing; he will surely pass through a thousand births.
uttar.109.cau4: But the unbearable pain that comes with being born and dying will not touch him in the least.
In no birth will his knowledge fade. Śūdra, listen: my word holds true.
uttar.109.cau5: You were born in Śrī Rāma's city, and then you set your mind on serving me.
Through the power of that city and through my grace, devotion to Śrī Rāma will arise in your heart.
uttar.109.cau6: Now hear my true words, brother: serving the Brahmins is the vow that pleases Śrī Hari.
Never again insult a Brahmin; know the saints to be equal to the infinite Lord.
uttar.109.cau7: Indra's thunderbolt, my great trident, the rod of Death and the dreadful discus of Śrī Hari:
one whom these cannot kill is burnt up in the fire of hostility to Brahmins.
uttar.109.cau8: Keep this discernment in your mind, and nothing in the world will be beyond your reach.
And I give you one more blessing: your going will be unhindered everywhere.
uttar.109.do109क: Hearing Śiva's words, my guru rejoiced and said: So be it.
Then he counselled me and went home, keeping Śiva's feet in his heart.
uttar.109.do109ख: Driven by time, I went to the Vindhya mountains and became a serpent.
Then, when some time had passed, I left that body without any struggle.
uttar.109.do109ग: Garuḍa, mount of Hari, whatever body I took I would lay down again with ease,
as a man puts on new clothes and casts off the old.
uttar.109.do109घ: Śiva kept the rule of the Veda, and I did not suffer.
In this way, Garuḍa, I took many bodies, yet my knowledge never left me.
uttar.110.cau1: Whatever body I took, beast or bird, god or man, in each I kept up the worship of Śrī Rāma.
One pain I can never forget: the gentle, gracious nature of my guru.
uttar.110.cau2: My last body was that of a Brahmin, which the Purāṇas and the Vedas declare hard even for the gods to win.
There too I played among the boys, acting out all the deeds of Śrī Rāma.
uttar.110.cau3: When I grew up, my father taught me; I understood, listened and pondered, but none of it appealed to me.
Every desire had fled my mind; I was absorbed in Śrī Rāma's feet alone.
uttar.110.cau4: Tell me, Garuḍa, who would be so unlucky as to leave the cow of plenty of the gods and tend a she-ass?
Lost in love, I cared for nothing else; my father wore himself out teaching me.
uttar.110.cau5: When my father and mother were taken by death, I went to the forest to worship the protector of his people.
Wherever in the woods I came upon great sages, I would go to their hermitages, one after another, and bow my head.
uttar.110.cau6: I would ask them the tales of Śrī Rāma's virtues; they would tell them, Garuḍa, and I would listen in delight.
So I roamed, hearing the virtues of Śrī Hari recounted, and by Śiva's grace nothing stopped my way.
uttar.110.cau7: The three deep-rooted cravings fell away from me, and one longing grew strong in my heart:
only when I see the lotus feet of Śrī Rāma shall I count my birth fulfilled.
uttar.110.cau8: Every sage I asked would tell me that God is made up of all beings.
The doctrine of the attributeless did not please me; love for Brahman with attributes grew ever stronger in my heart.
uttar.110.do110क: Remembering my guru's words, my mind was fixed on Śrī Rāma's feet.
I roamed singing the glory of Śrī Rāma, my love new at every moment.
uttar.110.do110ख: The sage Lomaśa was seated under a banyan, in its shade, on the summit of Meru.
When I saw him I bowed my head at his feet and spoke very humbly.
uttar.110.do110ग: King of birds, the kind sage heard my humble, gentle words,
and asked me courteously: Brahmin, what brings you here?
uttar.110.do110घ: Then I said: Treasury of mercy, you know all things and are wise.
Revered one, teach me the worship of Brahman with attributes.
uttar.111.cau1: Then, Garuḍa, the great sage told me with reverence something of the story of Śrī Rāma's virtues.
And that sage of realised knowledge, absorbed in the knowledge of Brahman, judging me a most fit recipient,
uttar.111.cau2: began to teach me about Brahman: it is unborn, one without a second, without attributes, the lord of the heart;
without parts, without desire, without name and without form; it is known only by experience, it is undivided, and nothing compares with it.
uttar.111.cau3: It is beyond the reach of mind and senses, stainless, imperishable, changeless, boundless, a mass of joy.
You are That, the Vedas sing; between it and you there is no difference, as there is none between water and its wave.
uttar.111.cau4: The sage explained it to me in many ways, but the doctrine of the attributeless would not enter my heart.
Once more I spoke, my head bowed at his feet: Great sage, teach me the worship of the Lord with attributes.
uttar.111.cau5: My mind is a fish in the water of devotion to Śrī Rāma; how could it live apart from it, wise and great sage?
Be kind and give me that teaching by which, with my own eyes, I may see Śrī Rāma.
uttar.111.cau6: When I have seen the Lord of Avadh to my eyes' content, then I will hear the teaching on the attributeless.
The sage, after telling once more the peerless story of Śrī Hari, refuted the view of the Lord with attributes and set forth the attributeless.
uttar.111.cau7: Then I would push aside the view of the attributeless and argue, stubborn beyond measure, for the Lord with attributes.
I answered him and answered back, and signs of anger showed in the sage's body.
uttar.111.cau8: Listen, my lord: when much disrespect is shown, anger springs up even in the hearts of the wise.
If someone rubs sandalwood too hard, even from it fire breaks out.
uttar.111.do111क: Again and again the sage, in anger, expounded knowledge,
while I sat there and turned over many thoughts in my own mind:
uttar.111.do111ख: Can anger arise where there is no sense of duality? Can duality exist without ignorance?
Can the soul, in the grip of māyā, limited and inert, be the equal of God?
uttar.112.cau1: Does sorrow ever come to one who looks to the good of all? Can poverty touch one who owns the touchstone?
Can those who wrong others live free of fear? And do the lustful stay without a stain?
uttar.112.cau2: Does anyone's line survive harm done to a Brahmin? Once one has known one's own true nature, is there still karma?
Has good sense ever sprung up in anyone in the company of the wicked? Does one who goes to another's wife reach a good end?
uttar.112.cau3: Do those who know the Supreme Self fall into worldly existence? Are those who revile Śrī Hari ever happy?
Does a kingdom last without knowledge of right policy? Do sins remain when the deeds of Śrī Hari are told?
uttar.112.cau4: Is holy fame won without merit? Does anyone earn ill fame without sin?
Is there any gain equal to devotion to Śrī Hari, which the Vedas, the saints and the Purāṇas sing?
uttar.112.cau5: Brother, to gain a human body and not worship Śrī Rāma: what loss in the world could equal this?
Is there any other sin like backbiting, Garuḍa, or any dharma like compassion?
uttar.112.cau6: In this way I kept weighing countless arguments in my mind, and did not hear the sage's teaching with respect.
When again and again I planted myself on the side of the Lord with attributes, the sage spoke in anger:
uttar.112.cau7: Fool, I give you the highest teaching and you will not accept it; you keep bringing answer upon answer.
You put no faith in words of truth; like a crow you are afraid of everything.
uttar.112.cau8: Wretch, your heart clings hard to your own side: become at once the lowest of birds.
I took the curse upon my head; I felt no fear, and no dejection came over me.
uttar.112.do112क: At once I became a crow; then, bowing my head again at the sage's feet
and remembering Śrī Rāma, the jewel of the Raghu line, I flew away in gladness.
uttar.112.do112ख: Umā, those whose love is fixed on Śrī Rāma's feet, who have left desire, pride and anger behind,
see the whole world as full of their own Lord: with whom, then, should they quarrel?
uttar.113.cau1: Kākabhuśuṇḍi said: Listen, Garuḍa: no blame at all lies with the sage; the one who stirs the heart is Śrī Rāma, the ornament of the Raghu line.
To try my love, the ocean of mercy made the sage's mind simple and unwary.
uttar.113.cau2: The Lord saw that in thought, word and deed I was his own; then he turned the sage's mind back again.
The sage saw my great gentleness of nature and my special faith in Śrī Rāma's feet.
uttar.113.cau3: Deeply astonished, he repented again and again, and the sage called me back with respect.
He comforted me in many ways, and then, glad at heart, gave me the mantra of Rāma.
uttar.113.cau4: The sage, a treasury of compassion, taught me the meditation on Śrī Rāma in the form of a child.
That lovely, joy-giving meditation delighted me greatly; I have already told it to you.
uttar.113.cau5: The sage kept me there with him for some time, and then he told the Rāmacaritamānasa.
When he had told me this story with reverence, the sage spoke again in gracious words:
uttar.113.cau6: Dear one, I received this lovely and hidden lake of Śrī Rāma's deeds by the grace of Śiva.
It is because I know you to be Śrī Rāma's own devotee that I have told you all of it in full.
uttar.113.cau7: Dear one, never tell it to those who have no devotion to Śrī Rāma in their hearts.
In many ways the sage instructed me, and I bowed my head at his feet with love.
uttar.113.cau8: Touching my head with his lotus hand, the great sage blessed me with joy:
Unbroken devotion to Śrī Rāma will dwell in your heart for ever; this, from now on, is my grace upon you.
uttar.113.do113क: May you always be dear to Śrī Rāma, a home of good qualities, free of pride;
able to take any form at will, dying only when you choose, a treasury of knowledge and dispassion.
uttar.113.do113ख: Moreover, in whatever hermitage you dwell, remembering the Blessed Lord,
there ignorance will not spread for a yojana around.
uttar.114.cau1: No sorrow born of time, karma, the guṇas, faults or one's own nature will ever touch you.
The many lovely secrets of Śrī Rāma, hidden and open, in the epics and the Purāṇas,
uttar.114.cau2: all of them too you will know without effort; may your love for Śrī Rāma's feet be new every day.
Whatever you wish for in your mind, by the grace of Śrī Hari nothing will be beyond your reach.
uttar.114.cau3: Listen, Garuḍa, steady of mind: when the sage's blessing had been heard, a deep voice of Brahman sounded from the sky:
So be it, wise sage, as you have spoken; he is my devotee in deed, mind and speech.
uttar.114.cau4: Hearing the voice from the sky, I was filled with joy; I was lost in love, and all my doubt was gone.
I made my entreaty to the sage and, receiving his leave, bowed my head again and again at his lotus feet;
uttar.114.cau5: then I came joyfully to this hermitage, having gained by the Lord's grace a boon that is hard to win.
Listen, Garuḍa: since I came to live here, twenty-seven kalpas have gone by.
uttar.114.cau6: I am always singing the virtues of Śrī Rāma, and wise birds listen with reverence.
Each time Śrī Rāma, for his devotees' sake, takes a human body in Ayodhyā,
uttar.114.cau7: each time I go and live in Śrī Rāma's city, and find my joy in watching his play as a child.
Then, Garuḍa, keeping Śrī Rāma's child form in my heart, I come back to my own hermitage.
uttar.114.cau8: I have told you the whole story of how I came to have a crow's body.
Dear one, I have answered all your questions; immense is the glory of devotion to Śrī Rāma.
uttar.114.do114क: This body is dear to me for this reason: in it love for Śrī Rāma's feet was born in me.
In it I had the sight of my own Lord, and all my doubts were gone.
uttar.114.do114ख: I held stubbornly to the side of devotion, and the great sage laid a curse on me;
yet I gained a boon that even sages rarely win: see the power of worship.
uttar.115.cau1: Those who know such devotion and yet forsake it, and labour for knowledge alone,
are dullards: they abandon the wish-fulfilling cow at home and wander, searching the milkweed for milk.
uttar.115.cau2: Listen, Garuḍa: those who turn from devotion to Śrī Hari and seek happiness by some other means
are fools of foolish deeds who would swim across the vast ocean without a boat.
uttar.115.cau3: Hearing Kākabhuśuṇḍi's words, Bhavānī, Garuḍa spoke joyfully and gently:
By your grace, my lord, there is now no doubt in my heart, no grief, no delusion, no error.
uttar.115.cau4: I have heard the many holy virtues of Śrī Rāma, and by your grace I have found rest.
One thing I ask you, my lord; explain it to me clearly, treasury of mercy.
uttar.115.cau5: The saints, the sages, the Vedas and the Purāṇas say that nothing is as hard to gain as knowledge.
That very knowledge, master, the sage taught you, yet you did not honour it as you honour devotion.
uttar.115.cau6: How great is the difference between knowledge and devotion? Tell me all of it, my lord, home of grace.
The wise crow was pleased to hear Garuḍa's words, and replied with respect:
uttar.115.cau7: Between devotion and knowledge there is no difference at all; both take away the suffering born of worldly existence.
My lord, the great sages do name some difference; hear it carefully, best of birds.
uttar.115.cau8: Knowledge, dispassion, yoga and realised knowledge, listen, Garuḍa: all these are male.
The power of the male is strong in every way; the female is by nature weak and of an inert kind.
uttar.115.do115क: Only the man who is free of attachment and steady of mind can give up woman;
not the man of desire, ruled by the senses, who has turned away from Śrī Rāma's feet.
uttar.115.so115ख: Even such a sage, a treasury of knowledge, gazing on the moonlike face of a doe-eyed woman,
falls under her sway, Garuḍa: woman is the māyā of Viṣṇu made manifest.
uttar.116.cau1: Here I take no side; I state the view of the Vedas, the Purāṇas and the saints.
Delusion does not come to a woman from a woman's beauty; this, Garuḍa, is a matchless rule.
uttar.116.cau2: Listen: māyā and devotion are both of the feminine kind, as everyone knows.
Then too, devotion is dear to Śrī Rāma, and māyā, poor thing, is no more than a dancer.
uttar.116.cau3: Śrī Rāma favours devotion; that is why māyā fears her so.
The one in whose heart devotion to Śrī Rāma dwells always and unhindered, peerless and free of all adjuncts:
uttar.116.cau4: seeing him, māyā shrinks back and can exert none of her power over him.
Considering this, sages of realised knowledge ask for devotion, the mine of every joy.
uttar.116.do116क: This secret of Śrī Rāma no one comes to know quickly.
Whoever knows it by Śrī Rāma's grace is never deluded, not even in a dream.
uttar.116.do116ख: Hear, most skilful Garuḍa, a further difference between knowledge and devotion,
hearing which one comes to have unbroken love for Śrī Rāma's feet for ever.
uttar.117.cau1: Listen, dear one, to this story beyond telling: it can be understood, but not described.
The soul is a part of the Lord, imperishable, conscious, stainless, by its nature a mass of joy.
uttar.117.cau2: That soul, my lord, fell under the sway of māyā and was caught like a parrot or a monkey.
A knot was tied between the inert and the conscious; though it is false, it is hard to undo.
uttar.117.cau3: From then on the soul has been bound to worldly existence; the knot does not loosen, nor does the soul find happiness.
The Vedas and Purāṇas have told many remedies, but it does not come loose; it only tangles more and more.
uttar.117.cau4: In the soul's heart the darkness of delusion is thick; the knot cannot even be seen, so how can it come loose?
Even when the Lord brings about such a circumstance, it may only now and then be undone.
uttar.117.cau5: Suppose that by Śrī Hari's grace the lovely cow of sāttvika faith comes to dwell in the heart;
the countless prayers, austerities, vows, restraints and observances, and the good dharma and conduct that the Vedas speak of,
uttar.117.cau6: are the green grass; when that cow grazes on it and, finding her young calf of devout feeling, lets down her milk;
with withdrawal from the world as the milking tether, faith as the pail, and the pure mind, one's own servant, as the cowherd;
uttar.117.cau7: having milked, brother, the milk that is supreme dharma, let him boil it well on the fire of desirelessness;
then cool it in the breeze of contentment and forbearance, and set it into curd with the starter of fortitude and calm.
uttar.117.cau8: With gladness let him churn it with the churning-stick of reflection, on the post of self-control, with the rope of truth and kind speech;
then by churning draw out the butter of dispassion, stainless, lovely and wholly pure.
uttar.117.do117क: Then let him kindle the fire of yoga and feed it with deeds good and bad;
when the dross of attachment has burnt away, let the intellect cool the ghee of knowledge.
uttar.117.do117ख: Then the intellect, which is realised knowledge itself, having gained that clear ghee,
should fill the lamp of the mind and set it firm on a stand made of evenness.
uttar.117.do117ग: From the cotton of the three states and the three guṇas let the intellect draw out the fibre of turīya, the fourth state,
then card it and twist it into a firm, tight wick.
uttar.117.so117घ: In this way let the lamp of realised knowledge be lit, a mass of radiance,
on coming near which pride and all the other moths are burnt up.
uttar.118.cau1: The unbroken awareness so'ham asmi (I am That) is the lamp's most brilliant flame.
The joy of knowing the Self gives a clear light; then the delusion of difference that worldly existence grows from is destroyed,
uttar.118.cau2: and the boundless darkness of delusion and the rest, the household of mighty ignorance, is dispelled.
Then that same intellect, gaining light, sits in the house of the heart and unties the knot.
uttar.118.cau3: If it can untie the knot, the soul attains its end.
But knowing that the knot is being untied, king of birds, māyā then raises many obstacles.
uttar.118.cau4: She urges on many ṛddhis and siddhis (riches and powers), brother, who come and tempt the intellect with greed.
By charm, force and trickery they draw near and blow out the lamp with the breeze of their garments.
uttar.118.cau5: If the intellect is truly wise, it knows them for its harm and will not even look at them.
If that obstacle does not stop the intellect, then the gods make trouble.
uttar.118.cau6: The doors of the senses are the many windows of that house, and at each of them gods have taken their post.
As soon as they see the wind of the sense-objects coming, they force the shutters open.
uttar.118.cau7: When that gale enters the house of the heart, the lamp of realised knowledge goes out.
The knot was not undone, the light was gone, and the intellect was thrown into confusion by the wind of the sense-objects.
uttar.118.cau8: Knowledge does not please the senses or their gods; their love is always for the enjoyment of sense-objects.
The wind of the sense-objects has bewildered the intellect; who then will light the lamp again in the same way?
uttar.118.do118क: Then the soul suffers once more the many pains of the round of birth and death.
Śrī Hari's māyā is very hard to cross, lord of birds; it cannot be crossed.
uttar.118.do118ख: Discernment is hard to tell, hard to understand and hard to practise.
If by pure chance, as a woodworm happens to carve a letter, one gains it, even then obstacles are many.
uttar.119.cau1: The path of knowledge is a sword's edge; one falls from it in no time, king of birds.
He who keeps to that path without a hindrance attains kaivalya, the supreme state.
uttar.119.cau2: Kaivalya, the supreme state, is very hard to reach, say the saints, the Purāṇas, the Vedas and the Āgamas.
Yet, my lord, when one worships Śrī Rāma, that same liberation forces its way to him unbidden.
uttar.119.cau3: As water cannot stay without ground, whatever ten million means one tries,
so, listen, king of birds, the joy of liberation cannot remain without devotion to Śrī Hari.
uttar.119.cau4: Considering this, wise devotees of Śrī Hari disdain liberation and are drawn to devotion.
Through devotion, without effort or labour, ignorance, the root of worldly existence, is destroyed,
uttar.119.cau5: as one eats for the sake of being satisfied, and the fire of the stomach digests the food.
Such is devotion to Śrī Hari, easy and joy-giving; who is so foolish as not to love it?
uttar.119.do119क: Without the feeling of servant and served, Garuḍa, one cannot cross worldly existence.
Weigh this settled truth and worship Śrī Rāma's lotus feet.
uttar.119.do119ख: He makes the conscious inert and the inert conscious:
blessed are the souls who worship Śrī Rāma, so mighty.
uttar.120.cau1: I have explained the doctrine of knowledge; now hear the power of the jewel of devotion.
Devotion to Śrī Rāma is a lovely wish-fulfilling gem; in whoever's heart it dwells, Garuḍa,
uttar.120.cau2: it is supreme light day and night, needing no lamp, no ghee, no wick.
The poverty of delusion does not come near, and the wind of greed does not put it out.
uttar.120.cau3: The darkness of mighty ignorance is dispelled, and the swarms of moths are all defeated.
Desire and the other villains do not come near one in whose heart devotion dwells.
uttar.120.cau4: For him poison becomes like nectar and a foe a friend; without that gem no one finds happiness.
The grave ailments of the mind, which hold all creatures in misery, do not seize him.
uttar.120.cau5: If the gem of devotion to Śrī Rāma lives in someone's heart, not a trace of sorrow touches him even in dreams.
In this world those are the crown of the wise who strive well to gain that gem.
uttar.120.cau6: Though that gem is there for all the world to see, no one gains it without Śrī Rāma's grace.
The means of finding it are easy, but luckless men spurn them.
uttar.120.cau7: The Vedas and Purāṇas are holy mountains, and the many stories of Śrī Rāma are the fine mines in them.
The good who know their secrets are the prospectors, a sound mind the pick, and knowledge and dispassion the eyes, Garuḍa.
uttar.120.cau8: Whoever searches for it with love finds the gem of devotion, mine of every joy.
My lord, this is the faith of my heart: greater than Śrī Rāma is the servant of Śrī Rāma.
uttar.120.cau9: Śrī Rāma is the ocean and the steadfast good are the clouds; Śrī Hari is the sandal tree and the saints the breeze.
The fruit of all is lovely devotion to Śrī Hari, and no one has gained it without a saint.
uttar.120.cau10: Considering this, whoever keeps the company of the good finds devotion to Śrī Rāma within easy reach, Garuḍa.
uttar.120.do120क: Brahman, the Veda, is the ocean, knowledge is Mount Mandara, and the saints are the gods
who churn it and draw out the nectar of the story, whose sweetness is devotion.
uttar.120.do120ख: With dispassion as shield and knowledge as sword, slaying the foes pride, greed and delusion,
the one who wins the victory is devotion to Śrī Hari; think it over and see, lord of birds.
uttar.121.cau1: Then Garuḍa, king of birds, spoke lovingly: Gracious one, if you have affection for me,
my lord, regard me as your own servant and answer my seven questions in full.
uttar.121.cau2: First tell me, my lord of steady mind, which body is the hardest of all to gain.
What is the great sorrow, and what the great joy? Consider this too and tell it briefly.
uttar.121.cau3: You know the inner nature of the good and the wicked; describe their innate ways.
What merit, renowned in the Vedas, is greatest? And tell me which sin is the most terrible.
uttar.121.cau4: Explain to me the diseases of the mind; you know all things, and your kindness to me is great.
Kākabhuśuṇḍi said: Listen, dear one, with respect and deep love; I will tell this teaching briefly.
uttar.121.cau5: No body equals the human body; all creatures, moving and unmoving, long for it.
It is the ladder to hell, to heaven and to liberation, and it gives the blessings of knowledge, dispassion and devotion.
uttar.121.cau6: Those men who take that body and do not worship Śrī Hari, but cling to the senses, grow base and baser;
they take bits of broken glass in exchange, casting the philosopher's stone from their hand.
uttar.121.cau7: There is no sorrow in the world like poverty, and no joy in the world like meeting the saints.
To do good to others in word, thought and deed is the very nature of the saints, king of birds.
uttar.121.cau8: The saints bear suffering for the good of others; the wretched wicked, to bring others suffering.
Like the birch tree, the kindly saints always endure great hardship for others' good.
uttar.121.cau9: The wicked, like hemp, bind others, and have their skin stripped and die in torment for it.
The wicked do others harm though nothing is in it for them, like the snake and the rat; listen, Garuḍa.
uttar.121.cau10: They ruin others' wealth and are ruined themselves, as hailstones beat down the crops and melt away.
The rise of the wicked brings the world distress, as does that of Ketu, the notorious evil planet.
uttar.121.cau11: The rise of the saints always brings happiness, as the moon and the sun bring joy to the whole world.
The highest dharma, known from the Vedas, is non-violence, and no sin is as heavy as speaking ill of others.
uttar.121.cau12: One who reviles Śiva or the guru becomes a frog, and keeps that body for a thousand births.
One who reviles the brāhmaṇas suffers many hells and is then born in the world in the body of a crow.
uttar.121.cau13: Proud creatures who revile the gods and the Vedas fall into the Raurava hell.
Those given to reviling the saints become owls, lovers of the night of delusion, the sun of knowledge gone from them.
uttar.121.cau14: The dull who revile everyone are born as bats.
Now hear, dear one, of the diseases of the mind, from which all people suffer.
uttar.121.cau15: Delusion is the root of all diseases, and from them in turn spring many pains.
Desire is wind, boundless greed is phlegm, and anger is bile, which always burns the breast.
uttar.121.cau16: If these three brothers make friends, the painful sannipāta (a fever of all three humours) arises.
The many cravings for sense-objects, hard to fulfil, are all those pains; who knows their names?
uttar.121.cau17: Attachment is ringworm, envy is the itch, and joy and grief are a host of throat diseases.
The burning at seeing another's happiness is consumption; wickedness and crookedness of mind are leprosy.
uttar.121.cau18: Egotism is a most painful gout; hypocrisy, deceit, pride and vanity are the guinea-worm.
Craving is a severe dropsy, and the three kinds of longing are a raging tertian fever.
uttar.121.cau19: Envy and lack of discernment are two kinds of fever. How far can I go on naming the many evil diseases?
uttar.121.do121क: Men die in the grip of a single disease, and these are many diseases, past all cure.
They torment the soul without end; how then can it find samādhi, inner stillness?
uttar.121.do121ख: Observances, dharma, good conduct, austerity, knowledge, sacrifice, prayer and charity,
and remedies by the million besides: yet with them, Garuḍa, these diseases do not go.
uttar.122.cau1: In this way all creatures in the world are sick, suffering from sorrow, delight, fear, attachment and separation.
These few ailments of the mind I have sung of; they are in everyone, yet rare are those who have perceived them.
uttar.122.cau2: Once recognised, these wicked ailments dwindle a little, but these tormentors of people are not destroyed.
Once they get the wrong food of sense-objects, they sprout even in the hearts of sages; what chance, then, for poor men?
uttar.122.cau3: By Śrī Rāma's grace all these diseases perish, if the means come together in this way:
faith in the words of the true guru, the physician, and for restraint, no longing for the objects of sense.
uttar.122.cau4: Devotion to Śrī Rāma is the life-giving herb, and a mind full of faith is what it is taken with.
Taken in this way, those diseases are surely cured; otherwise they do not go, though ten million remedies be tried.
uttar.122.cau5: Know the mind to be free of disease, my lord, when the strength of dispassion grows in the heart,
when the hunger for right understanding increases, new every day, and the weakness of longing for the senses has gone.
uttar.122.cau6: When the mind has bathed in the water of pure knowledge, devotion to Śrī Rāma fills the heart and stays there.
Śiva, Brahmā, Śuka, Sanaka and his brothers, and Nārada, sages skilled in reflection on Brahman,
uttar.122.cau7: are all of this one view, lord of birds: love should be given to Śrī Rāma's lotus feet.
The Vedas, the Purāṇas and every scripture say that without devotion to Śrī Rāma there is no happiness.
uttar.122.cau8: Hair may grow on a tortoise's back, a barren woman's son may kill a man,
flowers of every kind may blossom in the sky; still no being hostile to Śrī Hari finds happiness.
uttar.122.cau9: A mirage's water may quench thirst, horns may spring from a hare's head,
darkness may put out the sun; still no being turned from Śrī Rāma finds happiness.
uttar.122.cau10: Fire may even spring out of ice, yet no one turned away from Śrī Rāma finds happiness.
uttar.122.do122क: Ghee may come from churning water, oil may be pressed from sand,
but without the worship of Śrī Hari the ocean of worldly existence is not crossed: this truth is unshakable.
uttar.122.do122ख: The Lord can make a mosquito into Brahmā, and make Brahmā lower than a mosquito.
Seeing this, the wise give up doubt and worship Śrī Rāma.
uttar.123.shloka122ग: I tell you what is firmly settled, and my words are not false:
those who worship Śrī Hari cross over what is most hard to cross.
uttar.123.cau1: My lord, I have told the incomparable deeds of Śrī Hari, at length and in brief, as far as my understanding goes.
Garuḍa, this is the settled teaching of the Vedas: worship Śrī Rāma, setting every other task aside.
uttar.123.cau2: Leaving the Lord Śrī Rāma, whom else should one serve, who claims even a fool like me for his own?
You are realised knowledge itself, with no delusion in you; yet, my lord, you have shown me great kindness,
uttar.123.cau3: in that you asked me for the most holy story of Śrī Rāma, which delights the minds of Śuka, Sanaka and his brothers, and Śiva.
In this world the company of the good is hard to find even once, for a moment or for a short while.
uttar.123.cau4: Garuḍa, think it over in your own heart: was I fit to worship Śrī Rāma?
I, the lowest of birds and impure in every way, have been made by the Lord holy and known throughout the world.
uttar.123.do123क: Today I am blessed, deeply blessed, though lacking in every way,
for Śrī Rāma, knowing me as his own, has granted me the meeting with a saint.
uttar.123.do123ख: My lord, I have spoken as my understanding allows, and have kept nothing back.
The deeds of Śrī Rāma are an ocean: can anyone touch its bottom?
uttar.124.cau1: Remembering Śrī Rāma's many virtues, the wise Kākabhuśuṇḍi rejoiced again and again.
Then he said: He whose glory the Vedas have sung as neti, not this, whose might, majesty and lordship are beyond compare,
uttar.124.cau2: whose feet are worshipped by Śiva and Brahmā: his grace on me is his utmost tenderness.
Such a nature I neither hear of nor see anywhere; whom, Garuḍa, could I count equal to Śrī Rāma?
uttar.124.cau3: Seekers, adepts, the liberated, the detached, poets, the learned, the grateful, renunciants,
yogis, heroes, great ascetics, the wise, those intent on dharma, scholars and those of realised knowledge:
uttar.124.cau4: none of them crosses over without serving my Lord. To Śrī Rāma I bow, I bow, I bow.
Going to his refuge, even heaps of sin like me are made pure: I bow to the Imperishable.
uttar.124.do124क: His name is the cure for the sickness of worldly life and removes the three terrible torments;
may he, the compassionate one, be ever kind to me and to you.
uttar.124.do124ख: Hearing Kākabhuśuṇḍi's auspicious words and seeing his love for Śrī Rāma's feet,
Garuḍa spoke words full of love, all his doubt gone:
uttar.125.cau1: Hearing your words, steeped in the delight of devotion to Śrī Rāma, I have reached life's fulfilment.
A new love for Śrī Rāma's feet has arisen in me, and all the trouble born of māyā has gone.
uttar.125.cau2: In the ocean of delusion you became my ship; my lord, you have given me joys of many kinds.
I have nothing to give in return; again and again I bow to your feet.
uttar.125.cau3: Your every wish is fulfilled and you love Śrī Rāma; dear sir, no one is as fortunate as you.
Saints, trees, rivers, mountains and the earth: everything they do is for the good of others.
uttar.125.cau4: Poets have called a saint's heart like butter, but they did not know how to put it rightly.
Butter melts when it is itself heated; the holy saints melt at the sorrow of others.
uttar.125.cau5: My life and my birth have borne fruit; by your grace all my doubt is gone.
Always know me as your own servant. So, Umā, the best of birds said again and again.
uttar.125.do125क: Then Garuḍa, steady of mind, bowed his head at his feet with love,
and went to Vaikuṇṭha, keeping Śrī Rāma in his heart.
uttar.125.do125ख: Girijā, there is no gain to equal the meeting with saints,
yet it does not come without the grace of Śrī Hari: so the Vedas and Purāṇas sing.
uttar.126.cau1: I have told this most holy history; as soon as the ears hear it, the snares of worldly existence fall away,
and love arises for the lotus feet of Śrī Rāma, the wish-fulfilling tree of those who bow to him, the treasury of compassion.
uttar.126.cau2: Sins born of thought, deed and word leave those who listen to this story with ears and mind intent.
Pilgrimage and the whole range of spiritual practices, mastery in yoga, dispassion and knowledge,
uttar.126.cau3: rites of many kinds, dharma, vows and gifts, restraint, self-control, japa, austerity and many sacrifices,
compassion for living beings, service of Brahmins and of the guru, and the excellence of learning, humility and discernment:
uttar.126.cau4: of every practice the Vedas describe, Bhavānī, the fruit is devotion to Śrī Hari.
That devotion to Śrī Rāma, sung in the Vedas, few have won, and those few only by his grace.
uttar.126.do126: Devotion to Śrī Hari, hard even for sages to win, is gained without effort by those men
who hear this story continually, with faith.
uttar.127.cau1: He alone knows all, he alone has true worth, he alone is the knower; he alone is the ornament of the earth, a scholar and a giver.
He alone is devoted to dharma and the protector of his family, whose mind is given to Śrī Rāma's feet.
uttar.127.cau2: He alone is skilled in right conduct and truly wise; he alone has rightly understood the teaching of the Vedas.
He alone is a poet, a scholar and steadfast in battle, who leaves guile behind and worships Śrī Rāma.
uttar.127.cau3: Blessed the land where the Gaṅgā flows; blessed the woman who keeps faith with her husband.
Blessed the king who rules by right policy; blessed the Brahmin who does not stray from his dharma.
uttar.127.cau4: Blessed the wealth that takes the first course, giving; blessed and ripe the mind that is set on merit.
Blessed the hour spent in the company of the good; blessed the birth with unbroken devotion to Brahmins.
uttar.127.do127: Blessed is that family, Umā, listen: the world reveres it and it is supremely pure,
the family that brings forth a humble man wholly given to Śrī Rāma.
uttar.128.cau1: I have told this story as my understanding allows, though at first I kept it hidden.
Seeing the great love in your mind, I then told you the story of Śrī Rāma.
uttar.128.cau2: This should not be told to the deceitful and the stubborn, nor to one who does not listen with his mind to Śrī Hari's play.
Nor should it be told to the greedy, the angry or the lustful, nor to one who does not worship the Lord of all that moves and does not move.
uttar.128.cau3: Never tell it to one hostile to Brahmins, even if he is a king equal to Indra.
Those fit for Śrī Rāma's story are the ones to whom the company of the good is very dear.
uttar.128.cau4: Those who love the guru's feet, hold to right conduct and serve Brahmins: they too are fit for it.
And to one who holds Śrī Rāma dear as life, it gives a joy beyond all others.
uttar.128.do128: Whoever longs for love of Śrī Rāma's feet, or for the state of liberation,
let him drink this story with feeling from the cups of his ears.
uttar.129.cau1: Girijā, I have told you Śrī Rāma's story, which quells the sins of the Kali age and cleans the mind of its stains.
It is the reviving herb for the sickness of the round of rebirth; so the Vedas and the wise sing of Śrī Rāma's story.
uttar.129.cau2: In it are seven lovely steps, the paths to devotion to Śrī Rāma.
Only he on whom Śrī Hari's grace is very great sets foot upon this path.
uttar.129.cau3: Those who sing this story without guile find the wishes of their heart fulfilled.
For those who tell it, hear it and approve it, the ocean of worldly existence is no wider than a cow's hoofprint, and they step across.
uttar.129.cau4: Having heard the whole story, which delighted her heart, Girijā spoke in gentle words:
My lord, by your grace my doubt is gone, and a new love for Śrī Rāma's feet has arisen.
uttar.129.do129: Lord of the universe, by your grace I am now fulfilled.
Firm devotion to Śrī Rāma has arisen in me, and all my sorrows are past.
uttar.130.cau1: This auspicious dialogue of Śiva and Umā brings happiness and allays sorrow.
It breaks the bonds of worldly existence, destroys doubt, brings joy to the devotees and is beloved of the good.
uttar.130.cau2: Those in the world who worship Śrī Rāma hold nothing as dear as this.
Through Śrī Rāma's grace I have sung, as my understanding allows, this pure and lovely story.
uttar.130.cau3: In this age of Kali there is no other means: not yoga, nor sacrifice, nor japa, austerity, vows or worship.
Remember Śrī Rāma, sing of Śrī Rāma, and hear the host of Śrī Rāma's virtues always.
uttar.130.cau4: Poets, the Vedas, saints and the Purāṇas sing of him whose great vow is to make the fallen pure.
Mind, give up crookedness and worship him; who has ever worshipped Śrī Rāma and not found salvation?
uttar.130.cha1: Listen, foolish mind: who has worshipped Śrī Rāma, purifier of the fallen, and not found salvation?
He delivered many wicked ones: the courtesan, Ajāmila, the hunter, the vulture, the elephant and others.
Even those among the Ābhīras, Yavanas, Kirātas, Khasas, Śvapacas and others who are sin itself
become pure by uttering the Name but once; Rāma, I bow to you.
uttar.130.cha2: Those who tell, hear and sing this story of Śrī Rāma, the ornament of Raghu's line,
wash away the impurity of the Kali age and of the mind, and reach Śrī Rāma's abode without toil.
Whoever finds five or seven of its caupāīs charming and keeps them in his heart,
from him Śrī Rāma takes away the faults born of the five dreadful forms of ignorance.
uttar.130.cha3: He who is beautiful and wise, a treasury of grace, and loves the helpless,
is Śrī Rāma alone; who else equals him in doing good for no gain of his own and in granting liberation?
By the merest trace of his grace even dull-witted Tulasīdāsa has found supreme rest;
there is no lord anywhere like Śrī Rāma.
uttar.130.do130क: O hero of the Raghus, there is none as lowly as I, and none who befriends the lowly as you do.
Bearing this in mind, O jewel of Raghu's line, take away the harsh distress of my worldly existence.
uttar.130.do130ख: Just as a man of desire holds a woman dear, and the greedy hold money dear,
so, O Lord of the Raghus, O Rāma, may you be dear to me without cease.
uttar.end.shloka1: The Rāmāyaṇa, hard to fathom, which the Lord Śrī Śambhu, the great poet, composed long ago
so that ceaseless devotion to the lotus feet of glorious Śrī Rāma might be gained,
Tulasīdāsa, holding it to be absorbed in the name of Śrī Rāma, and to still the darkness within his own heart,
has likewise set it in the common tongue as this Mānasa.
uttar.end.shloka2: Holy, taking away sin, ever bringing good, bestowing realised knowledge and devotion,
removing the stain of māyā and delusion, utterly pure, brimming with the water of love, auspicious:
those who bathe with devotion in this Mānasa of Śrī Rāma's deeds
are not scorched by the fierce rays of the sun of worldly existence.
